docs.title: Kissi proper names
docs.text:
Kissi first names and surnames are written with the Kisiei alphabet like other words. The names given according to birth order, very frequent in the examples of the 1979 manual (Keita 1979) — Tamba, Saa, Fallo, Faya, Kumba, Sia, Finda, Teeva… — contain no special letter and do not change.

For a name that contained ty, nh, ny, è, ö in the old spelling, apply the same correspondences as for other words (see From the old to the new spelling). In official documents (civil registers, identity cards), the name may keep the French spelling already in use; it is then quoted as it is, without being respelled.

docs.title: Foreign proper names
docs.text:
The Bible (BKG) adapts biblical names to the Kisiei alphabet, but keeps letters that do not exist in ordinary Kisiei words, in particular r:

Name (French) In Kisiei (Bible) Abraham Abraham Israël Israɛl Égypte Esipte Jérusalem Yerusalɛm Benjamin Bɛnyamɛn

Note that:

  • French è becomes ɛ (Israɛl);
  • j becomes y (Yerusalɛm, Bɛnyamɛn);
  • z and soft g are replaced by Kisiei sounds (Esipte for Égypte).

Names of peoples take Kisiei class suffixes: Israɛlla “the Israelites”, Aarɔn-nda “those of Aaron”.

docs.title: Loanwords
docs.text:
Kisiei has borrowed words from Maninka, French, English and Krio. Once integrated, a loanword is written with the Kisiei alphabet and takes a class suffix like a Kisiei word:

sɛbɛ “book, letter” (from Maninka), volion “money”, rɛsɛn “grape” (from French), kafo “festival, meeting”.

In Southern Kissi, a loanword adapts to the Kissi syllable: a consonant cluster is broken up by a vowel, and a word that would begin with a vowel often receives an h; Hala “God” thus comes from Arabic Allah (Childs 1995, p. 64-65). Loanwords there mostly enter class o in the singular and la in the plural (Childs 1995, p. 163). Biblical proper names, by contrast, keep their consonant clusters (Israɛl, Esipte).

Rule

  • An integrated loanword is written in Kisiei spelling: do not use é, è, ou or ch in it (rɛsɛn, not raisin).
  • r may be kept in a loanword where it is pronounced (rɛsɛn).
  • A non-integrated foreign word (brand name, quotation) is put in italics and keeps its original spelling.

The varieties differ precisely in their loanwords: Kisiduei borrows from Maninka, Kpekeduei from Loma, Mende and Krio (Keita 1979, p. 8-10) (see Regional varieties). In a text intended for everyone, prefer the common Kisiei word when there is one.

docs.title: From the old to the new spelling
docs.text: Kisiei texts from the 1970s and 1980s, including Keita's manual (1979), are written in the old spelling. This page explains how to read them and rewrite them. The last section does the same for two older northern sources, Paulme's vocabulary (1940s) and the fables Sandara Kissia.

docs.title: Basic correspondences
docs.text:
These are the correspondences on the “new spelling” sheet Nouvelle orthographe kissi (tableau de correspondances) (s.d.), checked against the Bible (BKG):

Old New Old example New example Meaning ty c tyuaa cuaa child nh ŋ nhuèènu ŋuɛɛnu five ny ɲ nyumndan ɲumndan night è ɛ Lènnden → lɛŋnden country ö ɔ pomböö pɔmbɔɔ small, younger mb mb (unchanged) tyuaamböö cuaambɔɔ child

For capitals: Ty → C, Nh → Ŋ, Ny → Ɲ, È → Ɛ, Ö → Ɔ.

mb = nb?

The correspondence sheet says “mb = nb”. The Bible never writes nb: keep mb.

docs.title: What the basic correspondences cannot capture
docs.text: Applying only the table above to the roughly 700 words of the glossary and verb list of the 1979 manual, about four words in ten are found unchanged in the Bible. For the others, either the word does not appear in the Bible (vocabulary of daily life, illnesses, tools…), or the Bible's spelling differs on one of the following points.

docs.title: 1. ŋ at the end of a stem
docs.text:
The old spelling wrote n for both [n] and [ŋ] at the end of a syllable. The Bible distinguishes them:

1979 Bible Meaning Lènnden lɛŋnden country, land Tyinnde ciŋnde tooth Tyannda caŋnda hips Tinndo tiŋndo interval, space (1979: “island” (Keita 1979, p. 155)) Dièn diɛŋ the day after tomorrow nan “good” naŋ good

There is no mechanical rule: you need to know whether the stem ends in [n] or [ŋ] (see Consonants). When in doubt, look the word up in the Bible or in the lexicon of this guide.

docs.title: 2. Tones
docs.text: The old spelling did not mark tones. When rewriting, add accents only where the Bible puts them: on mí/mì, mó/mò, má/mà and a few other words (see Tone).

docs.title: 3. Relatives and referents
docs.text: The 1979 spelling writes relatives as separate words (Domaa n pendu vo sèsa) (Keita 1979, p. 88-89). The Bible attaches the referent to the last word of the phrase with a hyphen (kɔngɔ vesɛi fula-o). The description of Southern Kissi likewise analyses this marker as a suffix placed at the end of the relative clause (Childs 1995, p. 285-286). See Word division.

docs.title: 4. Errors and variants in the manual
docs.text: The typed manual contains typing errors and some forms specific to the author's variety. Before rewriting a word from 1979, it is best to check that it is not garbled (the transcription flags doubtful passages).

docs.title: Method for rewriting an old text
docs.text:
1. Replace ty, nh, ny, è, ö with c, ŋ, ɲ, ɛ, ɔ (without touching the French).
  2. Look up each word in the Bible or in the lexicon; if it is there, take that form (watch out for n / ŋ and vowel length).
  3. Rewrite the relatives with the hyphen.
  4. Add tone accents on the small words that carry them.
  5. Mark the words you have not found as “to be confirmed”.
flowchart TD
    T["1979 text<br><i>Tyuaa, Nhömpum, Lènnden</i>"] --> S1["1. Replace <i>ty, nh, ny, è, ö</i><br>with <i>c, ŋ, ɲ, ɛ, ɔ</i>"]
    S1 --> Q{"2. Is the word in the Bible<br>or in the lexicon?"}
    Q -- yes --> F["Take that form<br>(watch <i>n</i> / <i>ŋ</i> and vowel length)"]
    Q -- no --> M["5. Mark the word<br>“to be confirmed”"]
    F --> S3["3. Rewrite relatives<br>with the hyphen"]
    M --> S3
    S3 --> S4["4. Tone accents<br>on the small words"]
    S4 --> R["Text in the current spelling<br><i>cuaa</i>, <i>ŋɔmpum</i>, <i>lɛŋnden</i>"]
The steps for respelling a 1979 text.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: 1979 New spelling Meaning Tyuaa cuaa the child Söèi sɔɛi the word Nyèi ɲɛi the thing Hangullo hangullo the heat Yöngu ndu yɔngu ndu give him Nhömpum ŋɔmpum six Lènnden lɛŋnden the country

docs.title: Older northern sources: Paulme (1964) and Sandara Kissia
docs.text:
Two further northern sources predate the Bible and follow neither the 1979 spelling nor the current one:

  • Denise Paulme's vocabulary and texts (Paulme 1964), collected in 1945–1949 around Kissidougou and Guéckédou, use her own phonetic notation (her p. V): a bar over a vowel for length, a tilde for nasality, ü, ẅ and ty, ny. She marks many words G. (Guéckédou) or K. (Kissidougou).
  • Sandara Kissia, the fables published by the Protestant Mission of Kissidougou (Mission Protestante de Kissidougou s.d.), use an older missionary spelling (ty, ny, ŋg, gb, w, r).

The Lexique kissi–français (Lexique kissi – français s.d.) is typed in the current letters (c, ɛ, ɔ, ŋ, ɲ), without tones, but does not follow the Bible everywhere: it writes r for l, nb for mb (kunbi, Bible kumbi), nn where the Bible has ŋn (lɛnnden, Bible lɛŋnden), ki where the Bible has ci (kinbu, Bible cimbɔɔ), and often leaves out the i after s (sanie, Bible sianion). Much of it also repeats the glossary of the 1979 manual, typing errors included, so it does not always confirm a 1979 word independently.

Neither Paulme nor Sandara Kissia marks tones. The table below was worked out by comparing their words with the Bible's: about 60 of Paulme's headwords with the same meaning in the Bible, and every word of Sandara Kissia (with these rules, the share of its running words found in the Bible rises from 59 % to 80 %). The rules hold for most words, not all: always look the result up.

Old Bible Old example Bible Meaning ty c Paulme tyal cal sit, live ny ɲ Paulme nyunã ɲuna ask Paulme tũ, tü (plain tu usually stays tu) cu Paulme tũei, tũindo cuei, cuinndo axe, goat w at the start of a word, Paulme ẅ v Paulme wana, ẅiyo vana, vííyo person, orphan w between vowels wv (sometimes v) Paulme nawo, pevo; kowã nawvo, pewvo; koovan cattle, pig; blood u after a vowel at the end of a word w tau, Sandara gbou taw, kpow very, all w after a consonant u Sandara lwɛi luɛi enter y after a vowel i Paulme luɛy, pɛy luɛi, pɛi enter, the day before yesterday y between a consonant and a vowel i Paulme kɛndya, sendyo kɛndia, sendío health, shave gb, and often Paulme's b kp Sandara gbou; Paulme bɛro kpow; kpeloo all; bed Paulme md mnd Paulme kumde kumnde smoke r l: Kisiei does not distinguish l and r; some varieties (Kissidougou, where Sandara Kissia was written) say r where others say l, and the Bible always writes l (r only in names and loanwords; see Regional varieties) Sandara re, kɔraŋ le, kɔlan not, go ŋg, ŋk ng, nk Sandara yɔŋgu yɔngu give bar over a vowel (length) usually a double vowel Paulme bī, sā, pā bii, saa, paa catch, sheep, bone tilde (nasal vowel) at the end of a noun vowel + n Paulme balã, dumbulẽ, luã balan, dumbulen, lɔan hands, roots, sleep tilde at the end of a verb often nothing Paulme nyunã ɲuna ask ɛ, ɔ, ŋ, double consonants unchanged Paulme kɔllo, hɛlle kɔllo, hɛlle heart, salt

Further correspondences hold for many of Paulme's words but not all: her u is often the Bible's o (buryo “wound”, Bible booluu); her final -o is often -ɔɔ (namtano, Bible namtanɔɔ), as in agent nouns; her final -e is sometimes -en (bolle, Bible bollen); her ty- is sometimes ki- (tyallo, Bible kiallo); her y- is sometimes ɲ- (yuna, Bible ɲuna). Her mark /S./ means “south” (a southern word), not a third dialect.

Sandara Kissia and the Lexique write a pronoun and pila “self, alone” as one word (ndupila, yapilɛ); the Bible writes two words: ndu pila.

Guéckédou and Kissidougou

Where Paulme gives a Guéckédou and a Kissidougou form, the Bible often has the one closer to Guéckédou: Paulme tyɛyo (G.) / kyɛyo (K.) “house”, Bible cɛiyo. This is a tendency seen in a few words, not a rule; the Bible form decides.

No mechanical conversion

As with the 1979 spelling, these rules give a candidate, not the answer: vowels often differ too (Paulme kul “drink”, Bible kolɔɔ; Paulme luã “sleep”, Bible lɔan). A word taken from these sources goes into the lexicon in the Bible's spelling, with the form as printed kept in its source field; if the Bible does not have it, it is marked “respelled” (see How to read this guide).

docs.title: Punctuation
docs.text:
Punctuation follows the rules of French. The Bible (BKG) uses:

Sign Use Example . end of sentence Mí ɲɔɔ tosan lende. “And it was so.” Gen 1:9 , between clauses, in lists Sɛm, Ham a Yafɛt “Shem, Ham and Japheth” : before reported speech, a list Mí Hala dimi aa: «…» ? question Kuɛɛ nɛ n co yɛ? “Where are you?” Gen 3:9 ! exclamation, command Má cè laa nɔm! “Here is your wife!” Gen 12:19 « » reported speech Mó dimi aa: «Diomndo ndu.» ‹ › speech reported within other speech Gen 3:3 ( ) clarification, aside

docs.title: Reported speech
docs.text:
Direct speech is introduced by the verb of speaking followed by aa “that, this” and a colon, then placed in French quotation marks (guillemets):

Mí Hala dimi aa: «Ɲɔ́ɔ́ téngá!» Mí ɲɔɔ tèngà. “God said, ‘Let there be light!’ And there was light.” Gen 1:3

Rule

  • Quotation marks are written « » (and ‹ › inside), with no space inside the quotation marks in the Bible: «Diomndo ndu.».
  • The final full stop of the speech goes before the closing quotation mark when the quotation is a complete sentence.

Spaces

French typography puts a space before : ; ? !; the Kisiei Bible does not (dimi aa:, yɛ?). This guide follows the Bible. Both practices are readable; what matters is to be consistent within a text.

docs.title: Capitals
docs.text:
Use a capital letter:

  • at the beginning of a sentence: Mí Hala dimi aa…;
  • for proper names of people, places and peoples: Abraham, Esipte “Egypt”, Yerusalɛm, Israɛlla “the Israelites”;
  • for the names of God: Hala “God”, Mɛlɛka “the Lord”.

The letters specific to Kisiei have capitals: Ɛ, Ɔ, Ŋ, Ɲ (Ɲumma, Ɔ̀ɔ́). Titles and headings in the Bible are sometimes written entirely in capitals (KANDƆNNDO).

When a proper name takes a referent with a hyphen, only the first part takes a capital: Hala-o, Aarɔn-nda.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text: Numbers are normally written in words in running text (pilɛ, tiɔn, kɛmɛ); figures are used for numbering (chapters, verses, dates). See Numerals.

docs.title: A tone language
docs.text:
Kisiei is a tone language: the pitch of the voice on a syllable can change the meaning of a word or the grammatical value of a form. Two levels are distinguished, high and low, which can combine on a long syllable into high-falling and low-rising (Keita 1979, p. 17-18); Southern Kissi has the same inventory (Childs 1995, p. 43). Here are some minimal pairs (respelled forms):

Tone Word Meaning Tone Word Meaning high-fall. kɔɔ kind of snake ≠ low-rise. kɔɔ back low-rise. baa hand ≠ high-fall. baa price low-rise. bɔlɔɔ banana ≠ high-fall. bɔlɔɔ bag

Tone is also used in conjugation: i kela “I walk about (usually)” and i kela “I walked about” differ only in tone (Keita 1979, p. 18) (see Tense, aspect and mood).

docs.title: How the Bible marks tones
docs.text:
The old spelling marked no tones. The Bible (BKG) marks tone with accents:

  • the acute accent ( ´ ) for high tone: mí, náŋ;
  • the grave accent ( ` ) for low tone: mì, nàà;
  • on a long vowel, one accent per vowel: ndóò (high-low), màá (low-high), háá (high-high).

But it does not mark them everywhere: about one word in ten carries an accent. The accents are concentrated on two kinds of words.

docs.title: 1. Grammatical words whose tone changes their function
docs.text:
These are mainly the small words that link clauses. Their tone is always marked:

High tone Use Low tone Use mí “and (then)”, past narrative: Mí Hala dimi aa “And God said” Gen 1:3 mì “and (that)”, intended or future sequence: mì kɔngɔ vesɛiyo lo “and let the dry land appear” Gen 1:9 mó the same, + o “he, she”: mó sɛi “and he separated” Gen 1:4 mò the same, + o: mò vel naa “that he may resemble us” Gen 1:26 má the same, + a “they”: má kɔa yondoo nin “and they went into the bush” Gen 4:8 mà the same, + a: mà va kelaa “that they may fly” Gen 1:20

Other small words always carry their tone: háá “until” (to be distinguished from haa “these”), ndóò (past auxiliary, see Tense), ndáà “them” (beside ndaa “their”), tùú in le tùú “because”, tɔ̀a “all”.

docs.title: 2. Words that would be confused without an accent
docs.text: Some words carry an accent in almost all their occurrences, because they have a homograph: sálà “offering”, lasálàá “sacrifice”, siòònde “fear”, dɔ́ɔ́ngɔ́ “tent”, hɔ́ɔ́yɛi “freedom”.

docs.title: Other words
docs.text:
Common nouns, verbs and adjectives carry no accent: pɔmbɔɔ, cɛiyo, tosa, naŋ. When the same word appears in the Bible both with and without an accent, the form without an accent is generally by far the more frequent (naŋ rather than náŋ). In Southern Kissi, most nouns have only low tones, and the tone of verbs is set by the conjugation rather than by the word itself (Childs 1995, p. 54-55).

Practical rule

  1. Always mark the tone on mí/mì, mó/mò, má/mà and on the small words in the list above.
  2. Mark the tone on a content word only if it could be confused with another word in the context, and then follow the Bible's form.
  3. In all other cases, do not write an accent.
  4. One accent per vowel: a long vowel gets two (ndóò, háá).

Note

The exact tone rules of Kisiei (basic tones of words, tone changes in the sentence) are described neither in the 1979 manual nor in the Bible. They are among the open questions. For Southern Kissi they are described in detail (Childs 1995, p. 43-65, 91-98), but it is not yet known which of them also hold for Kisiei. The other older northern sources do not mark tone either: in Paulme (Paulme 1964) a bar over a vowel marks length and a tilde nasality, and neither the Lexique kissi–français, nor the Académie lists, nor Sandara Kissia carry accents.

docs.title: Intonation
docs.text:
The sentence also has an intonation (Keita 1979, p. 17): a question ends with a rise in the voice, a statement with a fall. In writing, this is shown simply by the question mark or the full stop: A hin? “Are you coming?”, I hin. “I am coming.”

In Southern Kissi, only the closed question (answer yes or no) ends with a rise; a question with a question word ends, like a statement, with a fall (Childs 1995, p. 60-61, 264).

docs.title: The seven vowels
docs.text:
Kisiei has seven vowels, like Southern Kissi (Childs 1995, p. 35). Two of them are written with letters that are not part of the English alphabet.

Letter Pronunciation Example Meaning i i of machine pilɛ one e close e, like ay in say but without the glide towards ee pelei foot ɛ open e, as in bed lɛŋ ground, earth a a of father bala hands ɔ open o, as in law (British thought) pɔmbɔɔ small, younger o close o, like o in go but without the glide towards oo yondoo bush u oo of food cuaa child front back close close-mid open-mid open i u e o ɛ ɔ a The seven vowels by tongue position (front or back, more or less open). Each can be long (doubled letter).

English speakers should keep every vowel pure: Kisiei e and o do not glide like English say and go.

Rule

Always distinguish e / ɛ and o / ɔ: they are different vowels, which change the meaning of words. Do not write é, è or ö: the è and ö of the old spelling become ɛ and ɔ (see From the old to the new spelling).

docs.title: Long vowels
docs.text:
A long vowel is pronounced for longer than a short vowel; it is written by doubling the letter: aa, ee, ɛɛ, ii, oo, ɔɔ, uu. Length changes the meaning of a word (Childs 1995, p. 37-38); it is the most frequent source of errors among learners (Keita 1979, p. 12).

Short Meaning Long Meaning velu beget veelu call yema sister yeema want bala hands baala work koma then, again kooma blood

Examples from the Bible: Mɛɛ Adam velu Sɛt “when Adam begat Seth” Gen 5:4; Mí Mɛlɛka Hala veelu vanapɔnɔɔ “The Lord God called the man” Gen 3:9.

docs.title: Final long vowel and the full form
docs.text:
Very often, the long vowel at the end of a word is not part of the stem: it is the class suffix of a noun or the infinitive marker of a verb. It disappears when the word takes its stem form:

Stem form Full form kala ndɔ “his/her mother” kalaa “the mother” fula “go out (he goes out)” fulaa “to go out, the going out” dio “eat (he eats)” dioo “to eat, the eating”

So do not “correct” kala ndɔ to kalaa ndɔ: the short form is the right one before a determiner (see Word division and Noun classes).

docs.title: Vowel sequences
docs.text:
Two different vowels can follow each other; they are written as they are heard, without a diaeresis or apostrophe:

  • ia, io, iɔ, iɛ: fuɲaa, dioo, tiɔn, ciɛɔn;
  • ua, uɛ, ui: cuaa, ŋuɛɛnu, kuí;
  • ɛi, ei, oi: cɛiyo, pelei, hoeiye.

These sequences are described in 1979 as diphthongs and triphthongs (Keita 1979, p. 11). In Southern Kissi, i and u before another vowel are pronounced as the semivowels [j] and [w], while sequences ending in i or u (ei, ɛi, oi, au…) have the length of a long vowel (Childs 1995, p. 39-42). The Bible (BKG) always writes them with the ordinary letters.

docs.title: Nasal vowels
docs.text:
When a vowel is followed by n at the end of a syllable, it is pronounced nasalised: an, ɛn, in, on, ɔn, un. No sign is added; simply write the vowel followed by n:

diolan “name”, mɛnndan “water”, nin “in”, kon “that…”, sɔɔn “words”, hun “come”.

In Southern Kissi, this final nasal is analysed as a consonant [ŋ] that nasalises the preceding vowel; it would continue earlier nasal vowels (Childs 1995, p. 88-89).

Note

At the end of a stem, the nasal sound can be [n] or [ŋ], and the Bible distinguishes them: nan “pull” (má nan Yosɛf “they pulled Joseph” Gen 37:28) is not naŋ “good”. See Consonants.

The sequences am, om, im… are not nasal vowels, but a vowel followed by the consonant m (Keita 1979, p. 13): yɔmndo is divided yɔm-ndo.

docs.title: Word division and the hyphen
docs.text: Knowing where a word begins and ends is one of the main difficulties in writing Kisiei. This chapter brings together the rules followed by the Bible (BKG).

docs.title: Full form and stem form of the noun
docs.text:
A noun has two written forms (see Noun classes):

  • the full form, with its class suffix, when the noun stands alone or at the end of a phrase: cɛiyo “the house”, yɔmndo “the tree”, diolan “the name”;
  • the stem form, without a suffix, when the noun is followed by a determiner, an adjective, a number or a possessor: cɛi kon “that house”, yɔm kon “that tree”, diola ndɔlan “his/her name”.

Rule

The stem form is a separate word, separated by a space from what follows. Do not write cɛikon or cɛi-kon.

Southern Kissi has the same alternation: the noun's suffix moves onto the word that modifies it (Childs 1995, p. 150-151).

docs.title: Grammatical words are written separately
docs.text:
Pronouns, auxiliaries, prepositions, demonstratives and possessives are written as separate words:

O co kɛndia le “he (she) is not well” 1 Sam 19:14 — o “he, she”, co “be”, kɛndia “in good health”, le (negation).

Mí Hala ca maa ɲɛ-tengaa naŋ “And God saw that the light was good” Gen 1:4.

The final negation le / te is also a separate word; write te after n, m, ŋ or l, and le after a vowel or w (see Negation; in Southern Kissi, te follows any consonant (Childs 1995, p. 89, 125)): La kei nanu le “do not pass through here” Num 20:20, Vana diinin nɔm te “no one will kill you” 2 Sam 19:24.

docs.title: The hyphen
docs.text: The Bible uses the hyphen a great deal (nearly 18,000 times). It has three uses.

docs.title: 1. The referent that closes a phrase
docs.text:
When a noun phrase ends with something other than the noun itself — a relative clause, a complement, a proper name — the noun's class is repeated by a referent (a class marker) which is attached by a hyphen to the last word of the phrase:

Group Referent Example class o (singular) -o, -ndo, -yo, -lo kɔngɔ vesɛi fula-o “the dry land that appeared” Gen 1:10 Kɔl Hala-o “the Spirit of God” Gen 1:2 o co paalen-ndo “the one that is the sun” Gen 1:16 class a (plural, persons) -a, -nda visia pɔmbɔa kela lɛŋ-nda “the small animals that walk on the ground” Gen 1:24 class an -an mɛmma co lebɛngu-an “the waters that are below” Gen 1:7 class e / i -e, -nde sɔɛi Mɛlɛka dimul ndu-e “the word that the Lord had spoken to him” Gen 15:6

The choice between -o, -ndo, -yo or -lo (and likewise -a / -nda, -e / -nde) depends on the end of the word to which the referent is attached: after a nasal write -ndo, -nda, -nde (lɛŋnden-ndo, nin-nda); elsewhere the simple form (fula-o, coo-an). The Agreement page gives these forms in detail.

1979 usage

In 1979, these referents are presented as separate relative pronouns (vo, ve, van, lan…), written after the verb (Keita 1979, p. 88-89): Domaa n pendu vo sèsa “the shirt that you bought has torn”. The Bible writes the same marker attached by a hyphen at the end of the relative clause; the form vo almost never appears on its own. Follow the Bible. The description of Southern Kissi points the same way: the noun's class ending is a suffix placed at the end of the relative clause (Childs 1995, p. 285-286).

docs.title: 2. Compound words
docs.text:
The hyphen joins the elements of a compound noun whose parts keep their form (in Southern Kissi, these non-fixed compounds are pronounced as separate words (Childs 1995, p. 216)): Cɛi-Hala-o “the house of God” Gen 28:17, fuɲa-mamaa “ancestor”, fonda-loamaa-lasálàá “altar (place where sacrifices are burnt)”, cɛi-kola “tent (house of cloth)”.

Very common compounds are often written as a single word: vanapɔnɔɔ “man”, vanalanɔɔ “woman”, halataalaa “sky”. See Compound nouns.

docs.title: 3. Reduplicated words
docs.text: A word repeated to express intensity, distribution or repetition is written with a hyphen: taw-taw “very much indeed”, ɲɛ-ɲɛ “anything at all”, yɛ́-yɛ́ “each kind”, bɛndu-bɛnduan “very big (ones)”.

docs.title: The prefix n'
docs.text: The nasal prefix n' is attached by an apostrophe to the following word: n'van tɔ́ “ten people”. See Consonants.

docs.title: Summary
Kisiei–English dictionary
docs.text:
This dictionary is generated automatically from the project's lexicon (6650 entries). Words follow the Kisiei alphabetical order (ɛ after e, ŋ and ɲ after n, ɔ after o); tone marks are ignored for sorting. The underline of each word shows its source, as elsewhere in this guide: Attested in the Bible (with a reference to one occurrence), Confirmed by a speaker, Respelled from an older written source (named after the entry), To check, or Southern Kissi (Childs 2000 only, not attested in the North). To look up a word from English, see the English–Kisiei index; for words grouped by theme, see the word lists. The full lexicon is also available as CSV, TSV, LIFT and CLDF in the repository.

Letters A · B · C · D · E · Ɛ · F · G · H · I · K · L · M · N · Ŋ · Ɲ · O · Ɔ · P · R · S · T · V · W · Y

docs.title: A
docs.text:
aa1 part. — quotative particle. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): also 'like, as' (comparison). Gen 1:3

aa2 pron. — he, she, they (before the verb, pluperfect). Lexique kissi–français, p. 3

akasia n. — acacia (pɛngɛn akasia 'acacia wood'). Exod 25:10

alaadio n. — radio set. Terminologie (arts), n° 207

-àlè part. — Southern Kissi only — emphatic tag (after commands, greetings). Childs 2000, p. 2

aliene n. — sky. Paulme 1964, p. 1

alumeco n. — matches. Paulme 1964, p. 1

amanndiee n. — almond, almond tree (yɔm amanndiee). Num 17:23

amoniɔmndo n. — harmonium. Terminologie (arts), n° 147

a … ni postp. — before, in front of (a … ni). Paulme 1964, p. 1

ansan n. — incense. Exod 25:6

antele interj. — polite greeting (at midday). Paulme 1964, p. 104

ava interj. — all right, well then. Judg 14:13

avokaanɔɔ n. — lawyer. Terminologie (histoire), n° 100

awa interj. — well, so (sentence-initial). Sandara Kisia, fable 4

a yandi interj. — please.

a1 prep. — with; and. Gen 1

a2 pron. — you (sg.); they (subject). Gen 1

docs.title: B
docs.text:
baabandinɔɔ n. — agent, official. Terminologie (histoire), n° 34

baakeo n., pl. bakɛian — thorny tree (medicinal bark). Other forms: bakio. Paulme 1964, p. 3

baalaa kɛu n. — strike. Other forms: baalaa yɔmnɔnndo. Terminologie (histoire), n° 370

baalaa n. (o), pl. baalalan — work; service; function, office. Other forms: baala, baalala. Gen 2:2

bɔ̀ŋgìóó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — black long-tailed bird (eats much rice). Childs 2000, p. 28

bɔ́ŋílɔ̃ŋ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — sucked in, drawn in (cheeks, stomach). Childs 2000, p. 28

bɔɔbɔɔvo adj. — multiple. Other forms: hɔlɔbioo. Terminologie (idéologie), n° 439

bɔɔbɔɔyɛi n. (i) — glory, majesty. Ps 96:7

bɔɔle adv. — perhaps. Gen 16:2

bɔɔluuo v. — make noise, roar; noise, uproar. Other forms: bɔɔluu. Isa 13:4

bɔɔŋiaa v. — gather, assemble; join together. 1 Sam 17:1

bɔɔŋian taasila laandoo n. — diphthong. Terminologie (langue), n° 130

bɔ́ɔ́ŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — red mud. Childs 2000, p. 30

bɔɔ3 n., pl. bɔɔlan — bush, thicket; (bɔ̀ɔ̀ n'yɔɔ) thornbush, bramble. Exod 3:2

bɔtáà n. (o) — fist. Exod 21:18

bɔtà n. — poison; to poison. Amos 6:12

bɔ̂ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — sound of splattering or shattering (egg, pot). Childs 2000, p. 25

bùèèŋèì adj. — Southern Kissi only — small (for one's age), stunted. Childs 2000, p. 31

búéèŋndó n. (o), pl. búéèŋndá — Southern Kissi only — striped (forest) rat. Childs 2000, p. 31

búê ideo. — Southern Kissi only — dented, smashed, sucked in. Childs 2000, p. 31

bugulo n. — eighth month (of the year). Paulme 1964, p. 13

bukpuo2 n., pl. bukpuva — cockroach. Paulme 1964, p. 13

bùŋbùŋndó n. (o), pl. bùŋbùŋndé — Southern Kissi only — small, uncommon tree. Childs 2000, p. 33

bùŋì lètèŋgéí n. (i) — Southern Kissi only — asthma. Childs 2000, p. 33

bùŋndó n. (o), pl. bùŋndáŋ — Southern Kissi only — (large) seed of a fruit; corn cob; cocoa bean. Childs 2000, p. 33

buuluuo v. — pierce, bore; break through; dig. Other forms: buuluu, buuluunin. Ps 22:17

bùùmbàá v. — Southern Kissi only — scrape. Childs 2000, p. 34

búúmbúúléŋ n. (le), pl. búúmbúúwé — Southern Kissi only — vine with red interior used as rope. Childs 2000, p. 35

buun n. — humps (of camels); hump (of an ox, of a person). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): unripe palm nut; hump. Isa 30:6

bùúŋndó n. (o), pl. bùúŋndáŋ — Southern Kissi only — hut, temporary palm-thatched shelter; cave. Childs 2000, p. 35

buusial v. — bring up (a matter) again with someone, speak of. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): restart (a discussion); remind someone. Deut 3:26

búúù ideo. — Southern Kissi only — copiously, abundantly. Childs 2000, p. 35

bùwàá v. — Southern Kissi only — hem. Childs 2000, p. 36

bu v. — scrape; clear stumps. Paulme 1964, p. 13

caleholen n. (len) — melon. Lexique kissi–français, p. 8

candɔɔ v. — praise, honour, esteem; praise. Other forms: candu. Job 29:11

canyɛi n. (i) — friendship; kindness, alliance. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): friendship; friend, lover. Gen 50:21

can v. — get up, set out; fly off. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): get up, arise; also grow, grow up. Other forms: cannin. Gen 12:9

caŋɛi n. — fringe. Terminologie (arts), n° 124

càŋgàbìnèìyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — long-handled cooking spoon. Childs 2000, p. 38

càŋgúlló n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — species of catfish, small and thick. Childs 2000, p. 38

caŋmamɛmo n. — flowing tears, ritual mourning laments. Paulme 1964, p. 111

caŋnda n. — hip, loins. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): waist, lower belly. Exod 28:42

capo adv. — much, a lot (adverb of quantity). Keita 1979, p. 117

catiyo n. — sauce of pounded and boiled cassava leaves. Paulme 1964, p. 112

cawvo n. (o) — kind of tree (its fruit: caw). Other forms: caw. Lexique kissi–français, p. 9

cécéŋ- adj. — Southern Kissi only — young (of an adult). Childs 2000, p. 39

cédé ideo. — Southern Kissi only — sharp prick (thorn, needle). Childs 2000, p. 41

cekeleiyo n. — lead guitar. Terminologie (arts), n° 141

celianndo v. — manage to save or do something. Other forms: celian. Lexique kissi–français, p. 9

celullo v. — be fat, thick; (celulaa) fat, fattened. Other forms: celul, celulaa. Judg 3:17

cengoo adj. — supreme. Other forms: mɛɛlula bɛndan. Terminologie (idéologie), n° 604

cèŋgéí n. (i), pl. cèŋgóŋ — Southern Kissi only — pin-like part near a hen's tail (said to prevent mating); clitoris; wattles. Childs 2000, p. 40

cèŋgímèìyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — species of banana. Childs 2000, p. 40

cèŋgìó n. (o), pl. cèŋgìléŋ — Southern Kissi only — elephant grass (savannas, floodplains; used for ear problems). Childs 2000, p. 42

cèŋgòó1 n. (o), pl. cèŋgèí — Southern Kissi only — heartwood (hard, rot-resistant part). Childs 2000, p. 40

cèŋgòó2 n. (o), pl. cèŋgùá — Southern Kissi only — witness to the payment of the bride price. Childs 2000, p. 40

céŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — blacksmith's hammer (also used for preparing medicines). Childs 2000, p. 42

cèŋùlló v. — Southern Kissi only — smack one's lips (kissing noise to amuse a baby). Childs 2000, p. 42

céŋ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — smoothly, evenly (of an animal entering or leaving a hole). Childs 2000, p. 40

cɛcɛŋa v. — chatter. Lexique kissi–français, p. 9

cɛ cɔwvo n. — prisoner of war. Terminologie (histoire), n° 500

cɛɛlan nsɔɔ n. — chronology. Other forms: keelan nsɔɔ. Terminologie (histoire), n° 238

cɛɛlianndo n. — interference. Terminologie (langue), n° 214

cɛɛlian v. — be next to, be neighbours; (vanaa … cɛɛlan-nda) neighbours. Other forms: cɛɛlan.

cɛɛlun v. — fall, drop; fall (in battle). Other forms: cɛɛlɔnndo, cɛɛlunnin. Isa 5:25

cɛɛluu v. — bring down, fell; drip, fall (dew). Other forms: cɛɛluuo, cɛɛluunin. Judg 6:37

cɛɛŋaa v. — sharpen. Other forms: cɛɛŋa. 1 Sam 13:20

cɛɛŋɔnndo v. — plead, beseech; supplication. Other forms: cɛɛŋun, cɛɛŋɔnnda. Gen 41:55

cɛi panio n. — house with a sheet-metal roof. Keita 1979, p. 142

cɛi puiyo n. — thatched house. Keita 1979, p. 142; Lexique kissi–français, p. 9

cɛi sɔva n. — henhouse under the veranda, lean-to. Paulme 1964, p. 96

cɛi tollo n. — house with a sheet-metal roof. Keita 1979, p. 142; Lexique kissi–français, p. 10

cɛiyo n. (o), pl. cɛilan — house ; house; household. Other forms: cɛi, cɛila, cɛinin. Variants: kiɛyo (Kissidougou). Gen 33:17

cɛ́kɛ́lɛ́ adv. — thoroughly, all over (wash, bathe). Lev 6:21

cɛllo adj. — positive. Terminologie (langue), n° 323

cɛlnun v. — be accepted, be approved; agree to, accept. Lev 1:4

cɛlɔɔ v. — accept ; accept, agree; listen to, obey. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): agree (to), concur. Other forms: cɛl, cɛlnin. Gen 3:17

cɛnkɔnɔɔ n., pl. cɛnkɔnɔa — parrot. Paulme 1964, p. 112

cɛŋio1 n. — elephant grass. Paulme 1964, p. 112

cɛŋio2 v. — make cry. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): cause to cry. Keita 1979, p. 114; Lexique kissi–français, p. 9

cɛɔ n. (o), pl. cɛa — slave, servant; captive. Other forms: cɛ. Exod 21:2

hangullo n. (o) — heat. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): heat, steam. Other forms: hangul, hangulu. Gen 8:22

hantenge interj. — sorry, excuse me. Lexique kissi–français, p. 17

hâŋndí ideo. — Southern Kissi only — snatching (take quickly). Childs 2000, p. 118

hàùdíí adv. — Southern Kissi only — this morning. Childs 2000, p. 118

háú-hàù ideo. — Southern Kissi only — stinging, burning sensation (sore, alcohol on a cut). Childs 2000, p. 118

hauvo n. — present tense. Terminologie (langue), n° 395

hau adv. — today, now. Gen 4:11

haw ba v. — overwhelm; be unable (because of circumstances). Lexique kissi–français, p. 17

háwèìyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — hour. Childs 2000, p. 119

háwèlè-hàwèlè ideo. — Southern Kissi only — rough, bumpy; burning hot. Childs 2000, p. 119

hawnɔnndo v. — get stuck; stand surety. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): be stuck. Other forms: hawnun. Prov 6

hawvo v. — block, trap, press. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): be stuck or trapped. Other forms: haw, hawnin. Exod 27:3

haw adv. — today. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): today; now, right away; again. 1 Sam 26:8

hàyàá v. — Southern Kissi only — iron (clothes). Childs 2000, p. 119

háyèìyé n. (i) — Southern Kissi only — (clothes) iron. Childs 2000, p. 119

ha det. — these (persons). Gen 7:1

hébè ideo. — Southern Kissi only — zooming by (pass). Childs 2000, p. 121

heelanndo n. — pride, haughtiness; one's glory. Prov 17:6

heeloo v. — lift up, raise. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): raise; praise. Other forms: heelu, heelunin, heelaa. Gen 13:14

heelɔnndo v. — exalt oneself, be proud; (sondoo heelɔnndo) speak arrogantly. Mal 3:13

heeluo v. — lift, raise. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): put up, raise, lift, erect. Other forms: heelu. Keita 1979, p. 110; Lexique kissi–français, p. 17

heelupifalnɔɔ n. — stage director. Terminologie (arts), n° 242

heelu tɛɛsiaa kaa n. — superlative. Terminologie (langue), n° 386

heende n. — shrub (Acacia ataxacantha). Paulme 1964, p. 34

hèèŋúúwó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — carapace, shell (e.g. of a snail). Childs 2000, p. 119

héèyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — animal pen, enclosure. Childs 2000, p. 120

helnɔnndo v. — go up, ascend, rise (into the sky). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): climb, ascend. Other forms: helnɔn. Judg 13:20

helɔɔ v. — go up, climb; height. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): climb, go up, rise; also mount, breed (animals). Other forms: hel, helnin. Gen 6:16

hèlùlló v. — Southern Kissi only — win (something) from someone (in a contest). Childs 2000, p. 120

hemndo n. (o), pl. hemndan — gourd, skin bottle. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): gourd for keeping oil or wine. 1 Sam 16:20

hendullo v. — give (an order) to; set (a snare) for. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): put or place something for someone. Other forms: hendul, hendulun. Gen 2:16

hengen adv. — a lot, much. Lexique kissi–français, p. 17

héŋbéndéŋ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — falling apart, collapsing. Childs 2000, p. 122

héŋgóó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — (old-time) high-piled female hairstyle. Childs 2000, p. 120

hèŋgúúwé n. (i) — Southern Kissi only — plant with edible white or yellow seeds (used in cooking). Childs 2000, p. 121

héú ideo. — Southern Kissi only — very big, enormous. Childs 2000, p. 121

he det. — this (i class). Gen 9:17

hɛɛnduuo v. — set up, place (several things); (sɔɔn hɛɛnduuo … coo) accuse. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): stack, place a succession of objects. Other forms: hɛɛnduu, hɛ́ɛ́ndùù, hɛɛndu. Job 33:10

hɛɛnndon n. — thistles, briers. Gen 3:18

hɛ́ɛ̀ interj. — aha! (ɛ̀ɛ̀ hɛ́ɛ̀, cry of joy or gloating). Ps 35:21

hɛiyo v. — winnow; sift; (fɛlɛ hɛyaa) winnowing fork. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): winnow, fan; also flutter; trick, fool. Other forms: hɛi, hɛinin, hɛyaa. Ruth 3:2

hɛ́lɛ́ŋ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — coming loose, popping out of its socket. Childs 2000, p. 122

hɛlihɛlio v. — sort repeatedly. Keita 1979, p. 110; Lexique kissi–français, p. 18

hɛli latandaa n. — regionalism. Terminologie (idéologie), n° 557

hɛlio v. — choose, select, sort. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): choose. Other forms: hɛli, hɛlinin, hɛlin. Exod 18

hɛli v. — choose. Other forms: hɛlinin, hɛlin. Gen 6:2

hɛlle n. — salt. Lev 2:13

hɛlul v. — choose for (someone); (hɛlulun) choose for oneself. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): select for someone (variant hɛlul). Other forms: hɛlulun. Exod 17:9

hɛlun v. — escape, survive. Other forms: helun, helunnin. Variants: hɛrun (with r). Job 1:17

hɛ̀lùŋndó n. (o), pl. hɛ̀lùŋndá — Southern Kissi only — water chevrotain (water deer). Childs 2000, p. 122

hɛlu v. — take (away), seize. Other forms: helu, hélú. Gen 27:36

hɛnan v. — please, be pleasing to. Other forms: hɛnanndo, hɛnannin. Gen 17:1

hɛngɛiyo n. (o), pl. hɛngɛilan — bowl, basin, dish. Other forms: hɛngɛi, hɛngɛila. Matt 23:25

hɛngɔɔ1 n. — chief's drum (to summon people). Lexique kissi–français, p. 18

hɛngɔɔ2 n. — wooden bowl, vessel. Ezek 4:9

hɛnudo n., pl. hɛnutan — gourd (for palm wine). Paulme 1964, p. 33

hɛŋgɛi-tòŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — old pot used for making soap. Childs 2000, p. 122

hɛ̀ù-hɛ̀ù ideo. — Southern Kissi only — panting (leopard, boar, angry person). Childs 2000, p. 123

hìàánànàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — unsteadiness, reeling. Childs 2000, p. 123

hìà-hìà ideo. — Southern Kissi only — laughing (ha-ha). Childs 2000, p. 123

hialu v. — take by stealth; slip away, disappear. Other forms: hialun, hialunin. Gen 27:35

hianndo v. — show preference. Other forms: hian. Lexique kissi–français, p. 18

híàŋ-híàŋ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — floppy, loose-jointed movement (a reeling drunk). Childs 2000, p. 124

hiawnanndo n. (o), pl. hiawnannda — passer-by, traveller; sojourner. Other forms: hiavannda. Lev 25:23

hiilaa v. — wail, lament; roar. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): hiccup; (plural hììlíá) sob or weep quietly. Other forms: hiila, hiiliaa. Gen 21:16

hiilɛi n. (i) — fury, rage. Ps 6:2

hiiloo v. — shake, toss, move. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): shake (transitive). Other forms: hiilu, hiiluu, hiiluunin. Ps 22:8

hiilɔnndo v. — tremble, be shaken; be troubled. Other forms: hiilun, hiilunnin. Isa 6:4

hììndìndòó v. — Southern Kissi only — swell up. Childs 2000, p. 124

hiiyo n. (o) — foam. Ps 46:4

hììyó v. — Southern Kissi only — make room for someone, let pass. Childs 2000, p. 125

hiko-hiko ideo. — (weep) sobbing. Gen 42:24

hilihiliei n. (i) — hiccup. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): to hiccup; to sob. Keita 1979, p. 161; Lexique kissi–français, p. 18

hílì-hìlì ideo. — Southern Kissi only — lumpy, thick. Childs 2000, p. 125

hìlló n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — (mushroom-shaped) termite mound. Childs 2000, p. 125

hiluan n. — craving (for food, meat), appetite. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): greed, excessive appetite (esp. for meat and fish). Variants: hiruan (with r). Deut 12:20

hilul v. — pant, be out of breath; be troubled, tremble. Variants: hirul (with r). 1 Kgs 10:5

hiluo v. — shake, wave. Other forms: hilu. Variants: hiruo (with r), hiru. Lexique kissi–français, p. 18

hindo n. — fever. Paulme 1964, p. 34

hindɔɔ1 n. (o) — boil; growth, growing. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): boil, swelling, lump, sore; growing up, coming to maturity. Exod 10:5

hindɔɔ2 v. — grow, grow up; swell, grow fat. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): grow, mature; also swell, bloat. Other forms: hindu, hindunin. Isa 53:2

hinia n., pl. hinilan — bed. Isa 28:20

hini v. — lie, lie down. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): lie down, rest, sleep. Ps 104:22

hinullo v. — come against, advance on; threaten. Other forms: hinul, hinulnin. Exod 14:10

hinul v. — attack, wage war on (… a cɔwvo). 2 Kgs 25:1

hiŋndo v. — shake, brandish, wield; (hiŋ … hɔlla) deceive, wrong; turn (something). Other forms: hiŋ, hiŋaa. Gen 3:24

hiŋnɔnndo v. — wander about; be agitated; be turned. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): be turned or stirred; turn around; become confused, go crazy. Other forms: hiŋnun, hiŋnɔn. Gen 37:15

hìɲáhíɲâŋndó v. — Southern Kissi only — move back and forth, to and fro. Childs 2000, p. 127

hiɲhiɲdo n. — "devil" (musical toy made of fruit discs). Paulme 1964, p. 34

hiovɔɔ laci n. — advance. Terminologie (histoire), n° 95

hiovɔɔ v. — pass, surpass ; pass; exceed, surpass; dominate. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): go by, pass. Other forms: hiow, hiaw, hiw, hiawnin, hiwnin, hiownun. Gen 1:16

hiownɔnndo v. — pass, go by (time); pass by. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): pass (middle). Other forms: hiownɔn. Ps 102:12

hio n. (o) — buffalo, bush cow. Paulme 1964, p. 34

hiɔlɔnndo v. — escape, get away. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): drop by accident, slip and fall; escape, slip away. Other forms: hiɔlɔn, hiɔlun. Isa 20:6

hiɔlɔɔ v. — take possession of, seize; invade. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): win from somebody, take away by persuasion, money or force. Other forms: hiɔlu. Deut 2:31

hiɔlundɔɔ num. — fourth. Job 42:16

híɔ́ɔ́dɔ́lɔ́ɔ́ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — stomach drawn in (from hunger, sucked in). Childs 2000, p. 128

hiɔɔlei n. — ransom. Terminologie (histoire), n° 513

hìɔ̀ɔ̀lɔ́léŋ n. (le) — Southern Kissi only — kind of mushroom (used in sauces). Childs 2000, p. 128

hiɔɔlundɔɔ num. — fourth. Other forms: hiɔɔlundɔ, hiɔɔlundɔlen, hiɔɔlundɔɛi. Exod 20:5

hiɔɔlu num. — four. Variants: nuɔlu (Kissidougou), ɲɔlu (Guéckédou). Gen 2:10

hìɔ̀ɔ̀nɔ̌ŋndó v. — Southern Kissi only — draw in one's stomach; swagger, bluff. Childs 2000, p. 128

hìɔ́ɔ́ v. — Southern Kissi only — singe (hair, feathers); cheat. Childs 2000, p. 128

hisɔp n. — hyssop. Exod 12:22

hiuo v. — pass; interpret. Other forms: hiu. Lexique kissi–français, p. 18

hivihivio v. — make pass repeatedly. Keita 1979, p. 110; Lexique kissi–français, p. 18

hivilacinɔɔ n. — progressive (person). Terminologie (idéologie), n° 525

hivio v. — make pass, send ahead. Other forms: hivi, hivia, hivin. Job 18:19

hivi v. — hand over, deliver to. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): lift over; circumcise; translate. Other forms: hivia. Matt 5:25

hiw ba v. — go too far, overdo, abuse; overwhelm; be in a hurry. Other forms: hiwba. Lexique kissi–français, p. 19

hiw v. — exceed, go beyond; surpass, be bigger than; be too much. Other forms: hiwnin. Gen 6:3

hiyahiyanndo adv. — one after another, alternately; hierarchy. Exod 28:34

hiyanndo v. — make a distinction; show partiality. Other forms: hiyan. Deut 1:17

hiyinɔɔ n. (o) — pilgrim. Keita 1979, p. 150; Lexique kissi–français, p. 19

hiyioo n. (o) — pilgrimage. Keita 1979, p. 150; Lexique kissi–français, p. 19

hobus n. — first farming task (cutting the grass of the lowlands). Paulme 1964, p. 34

hoeiye n. (i) — cold; breath, wind; malaria, flu ; air, wind; cold; breath. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): cold, cold wind; cold dry season; fever. Other forms: hoeyii, hoiye. Gen 31:40

hoeyii n. (i) — wind; breath. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): cold wind, cold season; fever. Gen 2:7

hókìíyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — week. Childs 2000, p. 129

hollo n. (o) — mushroom. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): mushroom; helmet. Keita 1979, p. 139; Paulme 1964, p. 34; Lexique kissi–français, p. 19

holnun v. — cling to, be joined to. Other forms: holnɔnndo. Gen 2:24

hòl-ŋ̀pèŋgòó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — edible mushroom (growing on a type of termite hill). Childs 2000, p. 130

holɔɔ v. — fix, attach, stick; climb (Keita); join; knock over. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): stick on, lean against. Other forms: hol, holnun. Exod 25:7

hòl-tìɔ́ɔ́ n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — termite mushroom (grows on termite hills). Childs 2000, p. 130

honnɔn ikalaa n. — marriage ties. Terminologie (histoire), n° 415

hòólan n. — fields, pastures, (farm) lands. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): old or abandoned farm, recently cultivated land. Other forms: hòóla. Isa 30:23

hóòlí ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (uprooted) completely. Childs 2000, p. 131

hoonde pron. — that one. Paulme 1964, p. 35

hoondo n. — leech. Prov 30:15

hòòŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — leech. Childs 2000, p. 131

hoo pron. — this one. Gen 3:3

hopɛw n., pl. hopiea — small yellow harmless water snake. Paulme 1964, p. 35

houvianndo v. — be pressed against one another. Lexique kissi–français, p. 19

hòùwáŋ n. — Southern Kissi only — potion made from hòùwó leaves (for constipation). Childs 2000, p. 131

hòùwó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — tree with hard white wood (for building). Childs 2000, p. 131

hovihovio v. — prick, pierce (repeatedly). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): prick many times. Josh 23:13

hovo n. (o) — kind of tree (bark used as medicine). Paulme 1964, p. 35

hoyaa n. — ambition. Terminologie (histoire), n° 42

ho det. — this (o class). Gen 2:16

hɔ́bɔ̀ adv. — Southern Kissi only — a lot, plentifully. Childs 2000, p. 132

hɔ́dèíyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — order (command). Childs 2000, p. 132

hɔlaa ɲaandiaa n. — grimace. Terminologie (arts), n° 133

hɔlaa piɔ́mndo n. — mask. Keita 1979, p. 144; Lexique kissi–français, p. 19; Terminologie (histoire), n° 419

hɔlaa n. — face; (o … hɔl) before, in the presence of. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): face; also sky. Other forms: hɔl. Gen 32:31

hɔlahiŋaa n. — dizziness. Lexique kissi–français, p. 19

hɔlla pusaa n. — emancipation. Other forms: kumbioo. Terminologie (idéologie), n° 277

hɔlla n. — face; side. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): face; sky. Other forms: hɔl. Gen 17:3

hɔlle kongelen n. — eyebrow. Lexique kissi–français, p. 19

hɔllo n. — tip, end (of a stick, sceptre); (o … hɔllo) before, against. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): point, tip, top, end. Esth 5:2

hɔlmaa postp. — (o … hɔlmaa) in the eyes of, in the sight of.

hɔ̀lndɔ̀ postp. — Southern Kissi only — close to, near, between. Childs 2000, p. 132

hɔlɔbioo n. — plural. Terminologie (langue), n° 339

hɔ́lɔ̀bí adv. — Southern Kissi only — a lot, a great deal. Childs 2000, p. 132

hɔlɔɔ v. — seize, snatch from someone's hands. Variants: hɔrɔɔ (with r). Lexique kissi–français, p. 19

hɔlta kalalan n. — hardness, ruthlessness; stinginess. Variants: hɔlta karalan (with r). Lexique kissi–français, p. 19

hɔlta vesɛlɛlan n. — boldness, courage; ruthlessness. Variants: hɔlta vesɛlɛran (with r). Lexique kissi–français, p. 19

hɔlten n. (len), pl. hɔltan — eye ; eye; (nɔ hɔlten … coo) watch over. Other forms: hɔlte, hɔlta. Exod 21:26

hɔlyɔnnɔnndo n. — ending, inflection. Terminologie (langue), n° 117

hɔnlesɛnnɔɔ n. (o) — flute player. Keita 1979, p. 145; Lexique kissi–français, p. 19; Terminologie (arts), n° 118

hɔnnɔ ɲɛsɔlaa n. — imperialist; imperialism. Terminologie (idéologie), n° 360

hɔŋndo v. — blow; sound (a trumpet); whistle. Other forms: hɔŋ. Lam 2:16

hɔ̌ŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — kind of forest bird (pheasant?). Childs 2000, p. 132

hɔŋnɔnndo v. — sound, be blown (trumpet). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): be blown. Josh 6:13

hɔ̀ɔ̀lɔ́ɔ̀ n. (o), pl. hɔ̀ɔ̀lɔ́a — viper, adder; snake. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): a poisonous water snake, a kind of adder. Other forms: hɔ̀ɔ̀lɔ́. Gen 49:17

hɔ̀ɔ̀néí n. (i), pl. hɔ̀ɔ̀nóŋ — Southern Kissi only — rice crust (at the bottom of the pot). Childs 2000, p. 133

hɔɔnie n. — rice crust at the bottom of the pot. Lexique kissi–français, p. 19; Sandara Kisia, fable 20

hɔɔnuo v. — weed. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): weed. Keita 1979, p. 110; Paulme 1964, p. 34; Lexique kissi–français, p. 19

hɔ́ɔ́pìó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — kind of snake (non-venomous). Childs 2000, p. 133

hɔ́ɔ́yɛi n. (i) — freedom. Exod 21:2

hɔ́ɔ́ n. (o), pl. hɔ́aa — child, offspring. Gen 4:1

hɔtte luɛyaalen n. — covetousness, greed. Terminologie (histoire), n° 212

hɔtten handɔɔ v. — control, supervise; control. Terminologie (histoire), n° 213

hɔvio v. — prick, sting (repeatedly). Other forms: hɔvi. Lexique kissi–français, p. 19

hɔvɔɔ v. — prick, pierce, thrust; inject. Other forms: hɔw. Lexique kissi–français, p. 19

hɔwvɔɔ v. — inject, thrust in. Keita 1979, p. 115

hɔ̂ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — stresses spilling (a liquid). Childs 2000, p. 131

huinden n. (len) — scabies. Keita 1979, p. 161; Paulme 1964, p. 35; Lexique kissi–français, p. 19

huinndon n. — scab, itching skin disease. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): craw-craw, a skin disease with mottled skin; smallpox. Deut 28:27

huinɔnndo v. — deceive oneself; (huinan) betray one another. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): fool or trick oneself. Other forms: huinan. Jas 1:22

hùíyé n. — whistle, hiss; (hɔŋ hùíyé) whistle, hiss. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): a whistle. Isa 5:26

huiyo v. — deceive, betray. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): cheat, deceive; also break a promise. Other forms: hui. Gen 29:25

hulio1 v. — pound fine, mash. Other forms: huli. Variants: hurio (with r), huri. Lexique kissi–français, p. 20

hulio2 v. — get dirty or dusty; (skin) flake. Other forms: huli. Lexique kissi–français, p. 19

hullan n. (lan) — brain. Keita 1979, p. 131; Lexique kissi–français, p. 19

hullo v. — blow (on); breathe into. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): blow on something; also lie to someone. Other forms: hul. Gen 2:7

hulma pɔmbɔan n. — brains (soft matter). Keita 1979, p. 131; Lexique kissi–français, p. 20

hulɔnndo v. — empty out, spill out. Other forms: hulun. 2 Sam 20:10

hulɔɔ v. — empty, pour out. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): throw away, spill, dump. Other forms: hulu. Isa 8:7

humboo adj. — white; (volin humbon) silver. Other forms: humbu, humbon. Gen 30:37

hunan adj. — rising, in flood (water); (mɛmma hunan) flood waters. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): flooded (mɛŋmà hùùnâŋ 'the flooding water'). Jer 46:7

hungulaa v. — enlarge, widen; exaggerate, blow up (a matter). Terminologie (histoire), n° 35

hunnun v. — (hunnun a) bring along, bring back. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): arrive, come by one's own power. 1 Chr 13:3

hunɔɔ v. — come ; come; (hun a) bring. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): come, arrive. Other forms: hun, hunnin, hin, hinnin. Gen 4:3

hùŋgòó v. — Southern Kissi only — pound grain (first of three poundings). Childs 2000, p. 136

huŋndo n. (o), pl. huŋndan — lowland, swamp; lowland rice field. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): swamp where swamp rice is grown. Keita 1979, p. 142; Paulme 1964, p. 35; Lexique kissi–français, p. 20

huo1 n., pl. hula — fallow field (to be farmed again). Paulme 1964, p. 35

huo2 n. (o), pl. húá — owl. Other forms: hua. Lev 11:16

huuluo v. — jump, leap. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): jump. Other forms: huulu, huulunin, huuloo, huuluu. Ps 68:4

ɗìàlìì-kòlà-níŋndé n. (i), pl. ɗìàlùŋ-kòlà-níŋndóŋ — Southern Kissi only — genitals (euphemism). Childs 2000, p. 76

ɗìàmbòó1 n. (o), pl. ɗìàmbùláŋ — Southern Kissi only — conversation, discussion. Childs 2000, p. 77

ɗìàmbòó2 v. — Southern Kissi only — chat, converse; lecture (someone). Childs 2000, p. 77

ɗìàŋkèlló n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — large driver ant (soldier). Childs 2000, p. 77

ɗìàŋòó n. (o), pl. ɗìàŋùéí — Southern Kissi only — kind of tree (used as firewood). Childs 2000, p. 78

ibungaa n. — governor (masa ibungaa). Other forms: ibunga. Hag 1:1

ibuŋ postp. — to, back to, with (o … ibuŋ). Gen 8:11

icali n. — residence; (va icali) live, dwell; seated, sitting. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): stay, live (cited as a form of càllé 'sit'). Judg 8:17

icɔllo n. — evening, night. Gen 1:5

icɔl adv. — in the evening, at night. Gen 1:5

idiiyo adv. — in the morning, early. Other forms: idii. Gen 19:27

idii adv. — in the morning. Gen 19:2

idio n. — midnight. Lexique kissi–français, p. 20; Sandara Kisia, fable 2

ifalenndo n. — ephod (doma ifalenndo, priestly garment). Other forms: ifalen. Exod 28:6

ihɛllan n. — sea (mɛmma ihɛllan). Other forms: ihɛlma, ihɛl. Gen 1:10

ihini adv. — lying down. 2 Kgs 9:16

ɗííyɛ̀-ɗííyɛ̀ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — cheeping of chicks. Childs 2000, p. 79

ii pron. — I (pluperfect). Lexique kissi–français, p. 20

iɲíí n. — pity, mercy; (tuinun … iɲíí) have mercy on. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): sorrow, pity, mercy. Jonah 3:10

ɗìòùwɔ̀ɔ́ v. — Southern Kissi only — be mushy, overcooked; be limp, unable to move (sick baby). Childs 2000, p. 83

ɗìɔ́ɔ́ n. (o), pl. dɛ̀ɛ́láŋ — Southern Kissi only — dough of pounded rice flour (with banana, sometimes honey). Childs 2000, p. 84

ipalaa n. — day(time), morning. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): afternoon. Other forms: ipala. Gen 1:5

ipala adv. — in the daytime. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): afternoon. Gen 1:5

ipulu n. — offspring; (naŋ ipúlú) be fruitful. Gen 1:22

isɛ interj. — greetings, hello. Gen 27:18

ɗìsìŋàá v. — Southern Kissi only — strike (on the head); squeeze hard; heap up. Childs 2000, p. 84

isiòòn n. — fear. Gen 15:1

isisi adv. — standing. Gen 18:2

isɔw n. — blemish, flaw. 2 Sam 14:25

ɗíù ideo. — Southern Kissi only — stresses throwing out. Childs 2000, p. 84

ivɔɔnde n. — evil, misfortune; danger. Prov 15:15

iyongban-yongbannde n. — (waters) surging, raging. Ps 46:4

kàá2 v. — Southern Kissi only — clear one's throat, hawk. Childs 2000, p. 140

kafalan n. — injustice; trickery, deceit, lie. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): cheating, deceit, trickery. Deut 24:17

kàfèìyó v. — Southern Kissi only — excuse; ask for leave or permission. Childs 2000, p. 143

kafilen n. — coffee tree. Lexique kissi–français, p. 20

kafio n. — coffee. Lexique kissi–français, p. 20

káfú ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (hang on, grab) tightly. Childs 2000, p. 143

kaiyo n. — thread. Lexique kissi–français, p. 21

kaka-kaka adv. — carelessly, in disorder; forcefully. Lexique kissi–français, p. 21

kákáù ideo. — Southern Kissi only — rough, bumpy. Childs 2000, p. 144

kalaa1 adj. — itself, the very (one); whole, entire. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): indeed, very, particular, itself. Other forms: kalalen, kalan, kalale. Gen 6:16

kalaa2 n. (o) — mother. Other forms: kala. Gen 27:11

kalaa3 v. — dig up, unearth. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): dig or pull out. Keita 1979, p. 110; Lexique kissi–français, p. 21

kalaa4 v. — paddle. Variants: karaa (with r). Lexique kissi–français, p. 22

kalabala n. — magic object (small lidded calabash of roots, leaves and fat). Paulme 1964, p. 41

kàlábùlùkáá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — worm-like non-poisonous burrowing snake. Childs 2000, p. 144

kàláfìɔ́ n. (o), pl. kàláfìá — Southern Kissi only — queen termite. Childs 2000, p. 145

kalakala adj. — difficult. Paulme 1964, p. 41

kàlàlíó n. (o), pl. kàlàlíá — Southern Kissi only — mother-in-law (husband's mother). Childs 2000, p. 145

kalamaa n. (o) — small spoon-shaped calabash; half calabash; rattle with a handle. Paulme 1964, p. 39; Lexique kissi–français, p. 21

kalamamaa n. — grandmother. Lexique kissi–français, p. 21

kalamulan n. — grams. Other forms: kalamula. Gen 24:22

kalande n. — calabash divination; divining ring. Paulme 1964, p. 41

kalaŋaa v. — be dug up, laid bare, turned up; pull out, bring up. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): (middle of 'dig up') be dug up, uprooted. Other forms: kalaŋan, kalaŋanin, kalaŋanndo. 2 Sam 22:16

kalaŋndo n. (o) — palm-fibre hamper ('kinja'); fetish worn at the neck or waist; remedy for beriberi. Paulme 1964, p. 39; Sandara Kisia, fable 6

kalayɛi n. — matriarchy. Terminologie (histoire), n° 420

kale n. — clan, clan name. Paulme 1964, p. 39

kalialahɔllo n. — burrowing insect (said to attack the eyes). Variants: karialahɔllo (with r). Lexique kissi–français, p. 22

kaliɲan n. — iron clapper (musical instrument of women griots). Paulme 1964, p. 41

kalio v. — wedge, brace (so it does not move). Other forms: kale. Lexique kissi–français, p. 21

kallante adv. — particularly. Lexique kissi–français, p. 21

kalɔɔ adj. — green, unripe. Lexique kissi–français, p. 21

kaluo adj. — hard, difficult. Other forms: kala. Variants: karuo (with r). Lexique kissi–français, p. 22; Sandara Kisia, fable 1

kamaa1 n. (o) — elephant. Variants: sɛmbaa (Kissidougou). 1 Kgs 10:18

kamaa2 n. — circle of people sitting (to play or tell a story). Lexique kissi–français, p. 21

kàmàcíŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — elephant rat (long-nosed). Childs 2000, p. 146

kamadolaa n. — beeswax. Paulme 1964, p. 40; Lexique kissi–français, p. 21

kamafoeinɔɔ n. (o) — photographer. Keita 1979, p. 145; Lexique kissi–français, p. 21

kamafoeiyo n. — gramophone. Terminologie (arts), n° 203

kamanda n. — door. Paulme 1964, p. 40

kamanduyo n. (o) — cast net. Paulme 1964, p. 40

kàmásɔ̀lɔ́ŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — variety of rice (said to have first grown from elephant dung). Childs 2000, p. 146

kàmàtìkèíyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — leafy vegetable like collard greens, seeds used for sauce. Childs 2000, p. 146

kamayɔlɔko n. (o) — war charm. Paulme 1964, p. 40

kambalaa n. (o) — insect; grasshopper. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): a large edible grasshopper. Lev 11:20

kambɛiyo n. (o), pl. kambɛilan — basket. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): large basket, hamper. Matt 14:20

kamilo n. (o), pl. kamita — slag; (pl.) iron ore. Paulme 1964, p. 40

kamɔyɛi n. — friendship, love. Lexique kissi–français, p. 21

kanapeo n. — sofa, canopy. Lexique kissi–français, p. 21

kandaa n. — catfish. Paulme 1964, p. 40

kàndàá1 n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — dam, fish trap. Childs 2000, p. 146

kàndàá2 v. — Southern Kissi only — dam up (a stream); beat, whip, flog. Childs 2000, p. 146

kàndàkpùpùèìyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — car, automobile. Childs 2000, p. 147

kandanndo n. — bad luck. Lexique kissi–français, p. 21; Terminologie (idéologie), n° 413

kanda v. — guard, protect. Other forms: kandanin, kandaa. Gen 3:24

kándéléŋ n. (le) — Southern Kissi only — braid of a woman's hair. Childs 2000, p. 147

kandenɔɔ n., pl. kandinda — apprentice. Paulme 1964, p. 40

kandia v. — bind up, mend (a calabash). Paulme 1964, p. 40

kandikandiaa v. — tie (a bundle) with cords. Other forms: kandikandia. Lexique kissi–français, p. 21

kandolan n. — bars, crossbars. Other forms: kandola. Exod 26:26

kandoncindo n. (o) — gum (of the teeth). Keita 1979, p. 131; Lexique kissi–français, p. 21

kandɔɔ v. — begin ; begin; beginning; (kandɔɔ …) starting from. Other forms: kandu, kandunin. Gen 1:1

kándùáŋ n. (ma), pl. kándùléŋ — Southern Kissi only — first palm oil. Childs 2000, p. 147

kándùléŋ n. (le) — Southern Kissi only — old worn dark-stained trousers of a child. Childs 2000, p. 147

kanduo n., pl. kandolan — wheel, circle; (pl.) small roof timbers. Lexique kissi–français, p. 21

kangalanndo n. (o) — obligation, duty; right. Terminologie (idéologie), n° 249

kangalan adv. — surely, certainly; compulsory, necessarily. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): truly; marks obligation, must. Variants: kangaran (with r). Gen 41:32

kangbaa n. — sideburns. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): sideburns; also an agreement with a deceitful person, promise. Keita 1979, p. 15

kangbonɔɔ n. — woman undertaker (digs the grave of women who died in childbirth). Paulme 1964, p. 41

kangboo n. (o), pl. kangboa — pigeon, dove. Other forms: kangbo. Gen 15:9

kangbɔnɔɔ n., pl. kangbua — initiate who has not done the kisitɔ. Paulme 1964, p. 40

káníéí n. (i), pl. kánííŋ — Southern Kissi only — money. Childs 2000, p. 148

kanikokoe interj. — cry of joy, congratulations. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): (noun) congratulations. Keita 1979, p. 120

kanimasinndɔɔ adj. — classical. Terminologie (langue), n° 62

kanite conj. — because. Lexique kissi–français, p. 21

kani conj. — because, for. Gen 2:3

kankira n. — trunk (box). Lexique kissi–français, p. 21

kankpoo n. (o) — wood pigeon. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): dove, pigeon. Keita 1979, p. 136; Lexique kissi–français, p. 21

kansa n. — braids on the sides of the head. Lexique kissi–français, p. 21

kan det. — those (persons). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): these (a class), labelled proximal. Gen 6:4

kaŋɛo n. — beeswax; honeycomb. Lexique kissi–français, p. 21

káŋgàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — bamboo or raffia mat (for ceilings and drying produce). Childs 2000, p. 148

kàŋgàlàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — deceit, cheating, greed. Childs 2000, p. 148

kàŋgbòkpòó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — gourd with ashes inside used in spinning cotton. Childs 2000, p. 148

káŋgóó n. (o), pl. káŋgóláŋ — Southern Kissi only — deep-set, sunken eyes. Childs 2000, p. 149

kàŋnda n. — paths, ways; tracks, footsteps. Other forms: kàŋ, kàŋndan. Ps 25:4

kàɲàá v. — Southern Kissi only — force open (mouth, door), check by opening (ear of corn); (kàɲàá hɔ̀ltéŋ) tease. Childs 2000, p. 149

kaolaa v. — love. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): love, be in love with. Other forms: kaola. Variants: kaoraa (with r), kaora. Gen 22:2

kaolianndo v. — love one another. Other forms: kaolian. Variants: kaorianndo (with r), kaorian. Rom 13:8

kapitɛnnɔ n. — captain. Other forms: kapitɛnnɔɔ. Lexique kissi–français, p. 21; Terminologie (histoire), n° 136

kásáá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — small reddish swamp mouse (edible). Childs 2000, p. 149

kasamba n. — late fonio. Paulme 1964, p. 41

kasa1 n., pl. kasalan — woollen blanket (from the Sudan). Paulme 1964, p. 41

kasa2 v. — refuse, resist. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): resist. Prov 1:24

kasio n. (o) — offence, fault; (del kasi) offend, sin against. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): rules of a (secret) society; the offence of breaking them. Other forms: kasi, kasila. Gen 40:1

kasi pisiaa n. — authorization, permit. Terminologie (histoire), n° 92

kasoo n. — squirrel. Lexique kissi–français, p. 22

kátáá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — chief's enclosure, inner compound. Childs 2000, p. 150

kattaa n. — fortress; (katta pɔmbɔɔ) small fort. Other forms: katta pɔmbɔɔ. Terminologie (histoire), n° 348

katta salasiiya n. — garrison. Terminologie (histoire), n° 359

katundo n. (o) — harmless earth-coloured snake. Paulme 1964, p. 39

katu conj. — because. Lexique kissi–français, p. 22; Sandara Kisia, fable 1

kaulen n. — bellows. Lexique kissi–français, p. 22

kauve n. (i) — (tobacco) pipe. Lexique kissi–français, p. 22

kàùwé n. (i) — Southern Kissi only — potion keeping evil spirits from a house or thieves from rice. Childs 2000, p. 150

kau ideo. — (take, snatch away) all at once. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): suddenness of taking, as an eagle snatching; used with 'take'. Isa 57:13

kàváá n. (o) — bright spot (on the skin). Other forms: kava. Lev 13:19

kava kava n. — medicine made with human fat (for power and health). Paulme 1964, p. 42

kavandio v. — preach. Other forms: kavandi. Lexique kissi–français, p. 22

kave1 n. — hunters' altar (upturned pot). Paulme 1964, p. 41

kave2 n., pl. kavon — liquid medicine, infusion; protection against witches. Paulme 1964, p. 41

kavo n. (o), pl. kava — large ape (chimpanzee?). Paulme 1964, p. 42

kawaa n. — skin blemish. Lexique kissi–français, p. 22

kawnalen n. — exodus. Terminologie (histoire), n° 326

kawve n. (i), pl. kavun — bean. Keita 1979, p. 139; Paulme 1964, p. 42 (G/K); Lexique kissi–français, p. 22

kayaa n. (o), pl. kayalan — basket. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): fish basket. Keita 1979, p. 159; Lexique kissi–français, p. 22; Terminologie (arts), n° 193

kayakayaa v. — surround, entangle; interlace. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): (ropes, vines) be tangled or twisted together; be overgrown. Other forms: kayakaya, kayakayan.

kayendo n. (o) — sedge. Paulme 1964, p. 42

kàyěŋndé n. (i), pl. kàyěŋndóŋ — Southern Kissi only — sword grass (vine?) with very sharp edges, hard to uproot. Childs 2000, p. 150

kâyìàŋ-kâyìàŋ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — lurching, wobbling (like a drunk). Childs 2000, p. 151

ka1 adv. — only. Lexique kissi–français, p. 20

ka2 part. — (after a reduplicated indefinite) whatever, of every kind. Exod 9:14

ká adv. — Southern Kissi only — for a long time, far, a lot. Childs 2000, p. 139

kebinɔɔ n. (o) — smith, metal worker, goldsmith (older name). Paulme 1964, p. 44

kèédei n. (i) — threshold. Gen 19:6

kééfáyɔ́lɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o), pl. kééfáyɔ́lúéí — Southern Kissi only — tree species (female in swamps, male on dry ground) with oil-bearing fruit and white latex. Childs 2000, p. 151

keeku v. — lead through, make pass through. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): pass through or by; experience; repeat. Other forms: keekan. Ps 106:9

keelaa v. — go about, walk about; (keela kɔllo) meditate, reflect. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): stroll, saunter, walk about. Other forms: keela. Ps 1:2

keeliaa v. — lead about; look around. Gen 13:10

keelian nsɔnɔ n. — chronicler. Other forms: keelian nsɔɔ. Terminologie (histoire), n° 237

kèèlúŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — a small species of bird. Childs 2000, p. 152

kééndéíyé n. (i) — Southern Kissi only — traditional razor blade. Childs 2000, p. 158

pɔntɛo n. (o) — first rains. Lexique kissi–français, p. 44

pɔntie n. — point, dot. Other forms: pɔntiye. Lexique kissi–français, p. 44

pɔ́ŋgɔ́sɔ̀ɔ́ adj. — Southern Kissi only — very small. Childs 2000, p. 310

pɔɔliaa v. — water, irrigate; (pɔɔla) wet, soak. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): soak, immerse in water, drench, water a plant. Other forms: pɔɔliaanin, pɔɔla, pɔɔlaa. Gen 2:6

pɔɔli adv. — from afar, at a distance, over there. Ps 139:2

pɔɔ1 adv. — first, for a while, meanwhile. Gen 27:44

pɔɔ2 n. — kind of tree (bark used for inhalations). Paulme 1964, p. 80

pɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o), pl. pɔ̀láŋ — Southern Kissi only — palm cabbage (eaten when rice is scarce). Childs 2000, p. 310

pɔpɔan n. — raindrops falling from trees or the roof. Lexique kissi–français, p. 44

pɔ̀pɔ́ɔ́ v. — Southern Kissi only — inspire, prompt (someone to do something). Childs 2000, p. 310

pɔpuo n. — kind of grass. Other forms: popuo. Paulme 1964, p. 82

pɔsɔkɔɔ n. — charm (healing those sick from yallo). Paulme 1964, p. 82

pɔsɔnio n. (o) — poison. Lexique kissi–français, p. 44

pɔ́sɔ́ŋúɲáá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — centipede. Childs 2000, p. 310

pɔsɔɔ n. (o) — small snail (species). Lexique kissi–français, p. 44

pɔtmanio n. (o) — purse. Other forms: pɔtɔmanilan. Lexique kissi–français, p. 44

pɔtɔlla n. — forced labourers; (pɔtɔlten) forced labour, servitude. Other forms: pɔtɔlten, pɔtɔlaa, pɔtɔlte. 1 Kgs 5:27

pɔtɔtɔ n. — plant (leaves used in ordeals). Paulme 1964, p. 82

pɔtɔtten n. — forced labour, corvée. Terminologie (histoire), n° 222

pɔ̀úwó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — white or grey clay; chalk; powder; gunpowder. Childs 2000, p. 310

pɔ́úwó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — swamp shrub whose leaves are used to wrap parcels (kola). Childs 2000, p. 310

pɔwlan n. (lan) — error, wrongdoing, sin. Other forms: pɔwla. Deut 11:16

pɔwvianndo v. — split up, divide among several. Other forms: pɔwvian. Lexique kissi–français, p. 44

pɔwvo1 n. (o) — tree (species) growing in lowlands. Paulme 1964, p. 82; Lexique kissi–français, p. 44

pɔwvo2 n., pl. pɔwva — warthog. Other forms: puwvo. Paulme 1964, p. 82

pɔwvo3 v. — divide, share out among. Other forms: pɔw. Lexique kissi–français, p. 44

pɔw v. — go astray, err; be at fault; lead astray; fall. Exod 14:3

pɔ̀yàŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — large tree with a bitter root (source of rattan). Childs 2000, p. 310

pɔ1 ideo. — be full. Lexique kissi–français, p. 44

pɔ2 n. — kind of tree. Paulme 1964, p. 80

pɔ́ adv. — far, far away; very high. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): far up or off, very high, at the top. Other forms: pɔ́-pɔ́. Job 22:12

pɔ̂ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — crack (breaking of a fragile object). Childs 2000, p. 308

puapilɛ n., pl. puapilɛa — neighbour, fellow; brother (fellow member). Gen 9:5

pua n. — father (term of address: 'Father!'), my father. Gen 22:7

púéè-púéè adv. — Southern Kissi only — a lot, plenty. Childs 2000, p. 310

púéíyé n. (i) — Southern Kissi only — pipe (for smoking). Childs 2000, p. 311

puilen n. (len) — tail. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): a brush of tied grass used by a praise singer, often replaced by a cow's tail. Other forms: puile. Exod 4:4

puiyaa v. — sprout, grow green, shoot again; greenery. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): sprout new growth, grow. Other forms: pui, puinin. Job 14:7

puiyo n. (o) — straw; thatching grass. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): new sprouts; thatch, grass cut for thatching. Judg 19:19

pùkéé ideo. — Southern Kissi only — whooshing sound of rice falling into a fanner. Childs 2000, p. 311

pùlàléŋ n. (le) — Southern Kissi only — line, column (of people, ants); ancestral line. Childs 2000, p. 311

pulen n. (len) — navel; umbilical cord; intestine. Other forms: pule. Keita 1979, p. 132; Paulme 1964, p. 83; Lexique kissi–français, p. 44

pule tando n. — thunderstone (neolithic axe, used to sharpen knives). Paulme 1964, p. 83

pulikola n. — woven cloth strip. Other forms: kula. Paulme 1964, p. 83

pullino n., pl. pullinda — albino; ghost. Paulme 1964, p. 83

pulon n. — entrails, intestines. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): stomach, intestines (plural pùlóŋ); also a woman's labour stage, a strip of cloth. Lev 8:21

pùlóó n. (o), pl. pùlúláŋ — Southern Kissi only — cluster, pod (kola nuts, palm nuts). Childs 2000, p. 311

pulɔnndo v. — wash oneself. Other forms: pulun, pulɔn. Variants: puru (Kissidougou), pilu (Guéckédou). Exod 2:5

pulɔn sɛllo n. — ritual ablution. Keita 1979, p. 150; Lexique kissi–français, p. 44

pulɔɔ v. — wash (people, body). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): wash, bathe. Other forms: pulu, pilu. Gen 18:4

pulta n., pl. pultan — ash. Exod 9:8

puluei n. — language of white people (French, English…). Variants: puruei (with r). Lexique kissi–français, p. 45

pululan n. — rope (of palm fibre). Variants: purulan (with r). Lexique kissi–français, p. 45

pululen n. (len) — gluttony, greed (for food), carousing; greedy, glutton. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): greed. Other forms: pulule. Variants: purulen (with r). Gal 5:21

púlùtù ideo. — Southern Kissi only — sound of grass uprooted, cloth tearing, a small motorbike. Childs 2000, p. 312

púlú ideo. — Southern Kissi only — quickly, suddenly. Childs 2000, p. 312

pumboo n. — nest, swarm (of bees). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): nest of wasps or of a kind of ant. Judg 14:8

pumbu le yulaa n. — trading company. Terminologie (histoire), n° 179

pumbu n. — settled place (icali o pumbu 'live in a fixed place').

pumndo v. — be full, satisfied; fullness. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): be full. Other forms: pum. Deut 8:10

pumpunndo n. (o) — large bird (species). Lexique kissi–français, p. 45

pum det. — a certain, some. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): also 'a few, part, a little'. Gen 2:10

pundaa n. (o) — blindness, dimness of sight; cataract. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): white filmy growth that causes cataracts and blindness. Gen 27:1

pùndóó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — hairy swamp rat. Childs 2000, p. 312

pundo n. — eleventh month. Paulme 1964, p. 83

pundɔɔ v. — knead, moisten (flour with oil); soak. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): squeeze, mash. Ezek 46:14

púndúkúlúŋ adv. — Southern Kissi only — very early in the morning. Childs 2000, p. 312

pundule n., pl. punduo — twins' herb (febrifuge). Paulme 1964, p. 83

púndùŋ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — splash (swimming, falling into water). Childs 2000, p. 312

pungaa v. — plunder, loot; plunder, spoil; seize (violently or quickly). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): fight or squabble over something (e.g. food); also blossom. Other forms: punga, pungapungaa. Ezra 9:7

pùŋpùùŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — insect, bug. Childs 2000, p. 313

púŋ1 ideo. — (idiiyo púŋ) very early in the morning. Gen 19:27

púŋ2 ideo. — Southern Kissi only — suddenly. Childs 2000, p. 313

pûŋ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — excessively (an overdone action). Childs 2000, p. 313

puo bɔlɔ n. — altar of the snake cult. Paulme 1964, p. 84

puo kunduo n. — slag (used in charms). Paulme 1964, p. 84

pùóó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — notch made when felling a tree. Childs 2000, p. 313

puɔ1 n. — kind of tree (bark used in kowã charms). Variants: pɔwvo (Kissidougou). Paulme 1964, p. 84

puɔ2 v. — bring back; marry. Lexique kissi–français, p. 45

pupabɛndo n. — grandfather. Paulme 1964, p. 84 (G)

pupayɛi n. — patriarchy. Terminologie (histoire), n° 460

pupulaa adj. — grey. Terminologie (arts), n° 137

pû-pù ideo. — Southern Kissi only — sound of an engine. Childs 2000, p. 313

pùsàá v. — Southern Kissi only — produce new fruit (pineapple, banana). Childs 2000, p. 313

pusianndo v. — stir; disturb. Other forms: pusian. Lexique kissi–français, p. 45

pùsìèí n. (i), pl. pùsɔ́ŋ — Southern Kissi only — buttocks, anus (vulgar). Childs 2000, p. 313

pute n. — small chili pepper. Other forms: pote. Paulme 1964, p. 84

puuloo n. (o) — earth, soil, ground; dust ; dust; mud, clay. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): mud, dirt, stoneless soil; mortar. Other forms: puulu. Gen 2:7

pùùlùéí n. (i) — Southern Kissi only — European or non-local language. Childs 2000, p. 314

puululen n. — native status (colonial), colonial yoke. Terminologie (histoire), n° 412

pùùlùléŋ n. (le) — Southern Kissi only — Western way of life, 'civilization'. Childs 2000, p. 314

pùùlùnɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o), pl. pùùlùá — Southern Kissi only — European, white person; someone following Western ways. Childs 2000, p. 314

puulun v. — set one's mind on, rely on; take note of, keep account of (sins). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): pay attention to, mark, mind. Ps 130:3

pùùlù- adj. — Southern Kissi only — foreign, European, Western, modern; governmental. Childs 2000, p. 313

puundulen n. (len), pl. puundun — root. Other forms: puundule. Keita 1979, p. 140; Lexique kissi–français, p. 45

puusiaa v. — scatter, disperse. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): scatter, spread about. Other forms: puusian. Gen 11:8

puusianɔɔ n. (o) — reactionary (Keita). Keita 1979, p. 148; Lexique kissi–français, p. 45; Terminologie (idéologie), n° 544

puusoo n. (o) — termite hill. Paulme 1964, p. 84; Lexique kissi–français, p. 45

puuvo v. — take, take away, snatch; take back, recover. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): take away, seize, snatch; also become engaged to, hire. Other forms: puu, puunin, puunun, puununnin. Gen 14:16

pùùwó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — assistance in a work-exchange agreement. Childs 2000, p. 314

púúwɔ́ɔ́ n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — goat-like animal. Childs 2000, p. 315

púvɔ́ɔ́ n. (o), pl. púwvɛa — gazelle, deer. Other forms: púvɛ. Deut 14:5

puya-puya n. — drizzle. Lexique kissi–français, p. 45

docs.text:
revolisiɔnndo n. — revolution; (revolisiɔnnɔɔ) revolutionary. Other forms: revolisiɔnnɔɔ. Terminologie (histoire), n° 554

rɛsɛnndo n. — vine, grapevine; (rɛsɛnndon) grapes. Other forms: rɛsɛn, rɛsɛnndon, rɛsɛŋun, rɛsɛnndan, rɛsɛnnda. Gen 40:9

robuo n. (o) — skirt, dress. Lexique kissi–français, p. 45
