docs.text:
saabandiinɔɔ n. — guard; (saabandiilen) the guard. Other forms: saabandiilen. Terminologie (histoire), n° 357

sààbándìínɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o), pl. sààbándìíyá — Southern Kissi only — chief's bag-carrier. Childs 2000, p. 315

sààbèíyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — bandage; lamp wick. Childs 2000, p. 315

saabelanɔɔ n. (o) — architect. Keita 1979, p. 145; Lexique kissi–français, p. 45

saa cuao n. — lamb. Lexique kissi–français, p. 45

saafɔɔ n. — scourge, plague. Terminologie (histoire), n° 343

saa kóndóó n. — ram. Keita 1979, p. 137; Lexique kissi–français, p. 45

saa laandoo n. — ewe. Keita 1979, p. 137; Lexique kissi–français, p. 45

saalaa v. — catch (something thrown), grab; join in (an argument). Other forms: saala, sala. Lexique kissi–français, p. 45

saalan v. — pay attention to, heed, care about; (… le) neglect. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): pay attention, do what someone says (middle of 'catch'). Matt 22:5

sáálɛ́ŋ n. (le) — Southern Kissi only — token (used in games). Childs 2000, p. 316

saalɔnndo v. — find; discovery. Other forms: saalun, saalunnin. Matt 7:7

sáàmbáŋ n. (ŋ) — Southern Kissi only — long-grained white rice variety. Childs 2000, p. 316

sààmɛ̀íyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — standard rice-measuring cup. Childs 2000, p. 316

saanaa v. — swim. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): swim, float; overflow (river). Other forms: saana. Ezek 47:5

sáándííyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — compound fence. Childs 2000, p. 317

saangiaa v. — mistreat, oppress, afflict; persecute. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): labour, work hard all the time. Gen 16:6

saangianɔɔ n. — oppressor. Terminologie (idéologie), n° 475

saangian v. — toil, labour, weary oneself (at). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): plural middle of 'tire'. Other forms: saangianndo. Prov 23:4

saani v. — plant, set out (a seedling). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): plant in a nursery; look beautiful; sign. Ezek 17:5

saan v. — begin, set about (doing). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): be held, hold oneself; start again (middle of 'hold'). Gen 33:4

saasaa n. — palisade, enclosure; fortification. Paulme 1964, p. 90; Terminologie (histoire), n° 104

saasalan n. — siege works, ramparts (pl.). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): barricade, fortified fence; an early women's dance. Isa 29:3

sáásàŋgbànɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — edible mushroom species. Childs 2000, p. 317

saasa n. — cage; henhouse. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): basket for holding chickens, chicken coop. Ezek 19:9

sáátátá ideo. — Southern Kissi only — straight on, right at. Childs 2000, p. 317

sààtóndóó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — dance troupe performing when a blacksmith dies. Childs 2000, p. 317

sààyìáŋndó v. — Southern Kissi only — wrap oneself in a cloth; shoulder (a bag). Childs 2000, p. 318

saa1 n. (o) — sheep. Gen 12:16

saa2 n. — October. Keita 1979, p. 152; Paulme 1964, p. 87; Lexique kissi–français, p. 45; Terminologie (langue), n° 446

saa3 v. — grab, seize, catch; hold; take; catch fire. Other forms: sa. Lexique kissi–français, p. 45

sabuo n. — agent (grammar). Terminologie (langue), n° 16

sabu n. — cause, reason; (le sabu yɛɛ) why; (le sabu kon) therefore. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): reason, cause, meaning; also an act of kindness. Deut 10:9

sadasiyaa soa n. — cavalry. Terminologie (histoire), n° 144

sadɛndo n. — excision rite (in the East). Paulme 1964, p. 87

saɛndu n., pl. sainda — monitor lizard. Other forms: saiɛndu. Paulme 1964, p. 87

safir n. — sapphire. Exod 24:10

sàfùéíyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — plant with sponge-like growths (used for scrubbing). Childs 2000, p. 318

safuna n. — soap. Lexique kissi–français, p. 45; Sandara Kisia, proverbe 79

sàkàá v. — Southern Kissi only — bend, twist; bend over (weeding); pull up (weeds). Childs 2000, p. 318

sàkàlàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — a tree species (inedible). Childs 2000, p. 318

sàkàlàpíóó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — stocks (for hands or feet). Childs 2000, p. 318

sàkàndàá n. (o), pl. sàkàndàláŋ — Southern Kissi only — salary, pay. Childs 2000, p. 318

sáká interj. — Southern Kissi only — exclamation of amazement or admiration. Childs 2000, p. 318

sàkéí adj. — Southern Kissi only — bent, twisted. Childs 2000, p. 318

sakiei n. (i) — sword. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): sword, dagger. Keita 1979, p. 156; Lexique kissi–français, p. 46

sákí-sákí ideo. — Southern Kissi only — burning hot; furious. Childs 2000, p. 318

saki n. — spear. Paulme 1964, p. 87

sàkómbɔ̀ interj. — Southern Kissi only — no! (strong disagreement). Childs 2000, p. 318

sàkó interj. — Southern Kissi only — no! (strong disagreement). Childs 2000, p. 318

sákpàà ideo. — Southern Kissi only — very long (stresses length). Childs 2000, p. 318

sakpoo adj. — upright, honest. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): (ideophone) straight ahead, erect; right away. Other forms: sakpo. 2 Sam 22:24

sakpoyɛi n. (i) — uprightness, integrity, equity. Job 2:9

salaa pansiɔnndo n. — pension. Terminologie (histoire), n° 465

salaa n. — wage, pay; pay; price. Other forms: sala. Variants: saraa (with r), sara. Gen 29:15

sàlàá n. (o), pl. sàlàláŋ — Southern Kissi only — type, kind; group, quantity. Childs 2000, p. 319

sálàá n., pl. sálàlan — sacrifice, offering; protection, charm. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): sacrifice; blessing; charm, talisman. Other forms: sálà, sálàla. Variants: saraa (with r), sara (Kissidougou). Gen 4:3

sálàbàlàà-sálàbàlàà ideo. — Southern Kissi only — very long (object). Childs 2000, p. 319

sálábú ideo. — Southern Kissi only — stretched out straight. Childs 2000, p. 319

salaka n. — altar against witchcraft. Paulme 1964, p. 89

salakokuo n., pl. salakokua — kind of turtle dove. Paulme 1964, p. 89

salalan n. — jokes. Variants: salaran (with r). Lexique kissi–français, p. 46

salamayɛi n. — splendour, glory, beauty; (sálámaa) handsome, graceful. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): favourite or cherished child. Other forms: sálámaa. Isa 60:21

salanndo v. — catch (again). Other forms: salan. Lexique kissi–français, p. 46

salasiinɔɔ n., pl. salasiiya — soldier; (salasiinɔ paandoo) rifleman. Other forms: salasiinɔ paandoo, sɔndasiinɔɔ. Terminologie (histoire), n° 577

salasiyaa kundaa n. — military division. Terminologie (histoire), n° 250

salatio n. (o) — authority, power. Variants: saratio (with r). Lexique kissi–français, p. 47

salavusoo n. — military service; (in compounds) military. Terminologie (histoire), n° 571

salavusuo n. (o) — military service. Variants: saravusuo (with r). Lexique kissi–français, p. 47

sálɛ́kpúúwó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — biting insect (like a mosquito). Childs 2000, p. 319

salikokoo n. (o) — dove. Variants: sarikokoo (with r). Lexique kissi–français, p. 47

salile n. — charm of the purifier (salino). Paulme 1964, p. 90

salillo n. (o) — cooking pot. Keita 1979, p. 159; Lexique kissi–français, p. 46

salino n., pl. salia — keeper of the kɔsɔa, purifier. Paulme 1964, p. 90

saliya n. — laziness; lazy. Paulme 1964, p. 87

sállo n. (o) — rubbish heap. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): rubbish or dust pile; also a pile of wood. 1 Sam 2:8

sâlló n. (o), pl. sâllá — Southern Kissi only — a fish species (shark?). Childs 2000, p. 319

salɔɔ v. — peel, weed. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): scrape (a surface). Other forms: salu, selu. Keita 1979, p. 115; Lexique kissi–français, p. 46

sámáá n. — concubine. Judg 8:31

sàmàkólòŋgíóó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — bed bug. Childs 2000, p. 319

samakoo n. — bedbug. Lexique kissi–français, p. 46

sámáláŋgàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — water genie, water spirit. Childs 2000, p. 320

sama n. (o) — credit, charge; sacrifice to the kɔya. Paulme 1964, p. 87

sambaa n. — gift. Lexique kissi–français, p. 46

sambɛiyo n. — last rice (of the paddy). Paulme 1964, p. 87

sámbɛ́íyó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — large rattan basket (about half a bushel). Childs 2000, p. 320

sambillo n. — excision rite, initiation (in the North). Other forms: sambilo, sambele. Paulme 1964, p. 87

sambino n., pl. sambila — initiated girl. Paulme 1964, p. 88

sámbìóó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — evil medicine, bewitching. Childs 2000, p. 320

sambiyo n. — sorcerer's (kuino) medicine, sometimes deadly. Paulme 1964, p. 88

sàmèlɔ́ɔ́ n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — a tree species (bad-smelling). Childs 2000, p. 320

samkpaa n. (o) — a kind of drum. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): drum about three feet high, held between the legs and played with the hands. Keita 1979, p. 163; Lexique kissi–français, p. 46

sàmsèllá n. (a) — Southern Kissi only — beads strung around a rattle (sasa). Childs 2000, p. 320

sàmsóá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — possessed person. Childs 2000, p. 320

samsɔa n., pl. samsɔala — charm (of the Guéckédou area). Paulme 1964, p. 88

samtaa n. (o), pl. samtalan — shoe, sandal. Ruth 4:8

sanaa adv. — straight, straight ahead, directly. Josh 6:5

sandaa1 adj. — righteous, just; (dɛnɛ sandaa) righteousness; honest, of good character. Other forms: sandaala, sandaalan. Gen 6:9

sandaa2 n. — story, parable, proverb. Lexique kissi–français, p. 46

sandamɔlinɔɔ n. — gendarme, policeman. Terminologie (histoire), n° 360

sandanɔɔ n. (o) — small red fish. Lexique kissi–français, p. 46

sandei1 n. (i) — justice, righteousness, equity; honesty, integrity. Ps 9:9

sandei2 v. — burn, blaze, shine (fire, lamp). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): burn, blaze, burst into flame. Exod 3:2

sande yoovo n. — kind of hibiscus. Paulme 1964, p. 88

sandiaa v. — throw out; stretch out straight; comb. Other forms: sandia. Lexique kissi–français, p. 46

sandiasayo n. — kind of weed, couch grass (?). Paulme 1964, p. 88

sàndíkìnɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o), pl. sàndíkìá — Southern Kissi only — vice-chief; assistant to the chief's head wife. Childs 2000, p. 320

sandiyo n. — kind of grass of rice paddies. Paulme 1964, p. 88

sandoo n. (o) — sour leafy vegetable (like Brussels sprouts); plant used to make a sour juice. Lexique kissi–français, p. 46

sando n., pl. saanda — driver ant. Paulme 1964, p. 88

sandu v. — be upright, be right; seem right (to someone). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): be straight, be honest; also be bright, blaze (lamp, fire). Other forms: sandunin. 1 Kgs 9:4

sangaa v. — be tired, toil; (sanga) tiredness, weariness; burden, pain. Other forms: sanga, sanganin. Gen 3:17

sangalaa v. — praise, glorify, exalt. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): praise, esp. by singing; also tie logs together to make a ladder. Other forms: sangala, sangalanin. Judg 16:24

sangala lekɛlɛmasaa n. — epic. Terminologie (histoire), n° 298

sangalanndo v. — boast, glorify oneself. Rom 1:30

sanganndo v. — tire oneself, labour. Other forms: sangan. Ps 127:1

sanga-sanga n. — ladder. Lexique kissi–français, p. 46

vɔmbaa v. — flatten tall grass to clear a path. Other forms: vɔmba. Lexique kissi–français, p. 62

vɔmbɔɔ n. (o) — saddle. Lexique kissi–français, p. 62

vɔmio n. — rice-flour pancake. Paulme 1964, p. 121

vɔmndo v. — beat (for game), hunt down. Other forms: vɔm. Hos 5:8

vɔngoo n. (o) — price, payment; purchase. Other forms: vɔngu. Gen 23:11

vɔ̀ngɔ̀ n. — reward, wages. Gen 15:1

vɔngullo v. — hand over, give up (cheaply); extradition. Ps 44:13

vɔŋɔndo n., pl. vɔŋɔnda — large toad living in water. Paulme 1964, p. 122

vɔɔca v. — knead, mix (flour with oil); (vɔɔcan) mixed. Other forms: vɔɔcan. Num 15:6

vɔɔciaa v. — crush, dash to pieces. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): squeeze; arrange. Other forms: vɔɔciaanin. 2 Sam 22:39

vɔɔlen n. (len) — dry season. Gen 8:22

vɔɔndo1 adj. — bad, evil, wicked; dangerous, harmful; ugly. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): bad, evil; also ugly (wɔ̀ùwó 'be bad or ugly'). Other forms: vɔɔn, vɔɔnda, vɔɔnnda, vɔɔnndan, vɔɔnndon, vɔɔnde, vɔɔnnden. Gen 2:9

vɔɔndo2 n. (o) — armpit. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): armpit; bosom. Gen 2:9

vɔɔsuuo v. — wipe, wipe away, blot out; forgive (sins); trim (lamps). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): wipe off, clean, erase; brush off, rub. Other forms: vɔɔsuu, vɔɔsuunin, vɔɔsu, vɔɔsun. Exod 30:7

vɔɔ v. — strike with a stone. Other forms: va. Lexique kissi–français, p. 62

vɔsiikɛmɔɔ n. — century. Terminologie (histoire), n° 574

vɔsio n. (o), pl. vɔsilan — year. Gen 1:14

vɔsɔkɔɔ n. — stony ground, rocky soil. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): gravel; gravelly upland soils. Mark 4:5

vɔsucala n., pl. vɔsulan — circle of stones on the village square, for sitting. Paulme 1964, p. 122

vɔsuo v. — wipe, erase. Other forms: vɔsu. Lexique kissi–français, p. 62

vɔvanndo n. — enmity, hostility; antagonism. Other forms: vɔvan. Gen 3:15

vɔvɛyo n. — epileptic. Paulme 1964, p. 122

vɔwlen n. (len) — ugliness, badness; worse; wickedness, danger. Other forms: vɔwle. Gen 41:19

vɔw v. — be bad, be ugly; be severe. Other forms: vɔwnin. Exod 9:24

vɔyɔn ideo. — (sit on the ground) dejectedly, slumped. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): describes relaxing or sitting. Isa 47:1

vɔ́yɔ́ɔ́ n. — leftovers, remainder (of food). Ruth 2:14

vɔ part. — not yet (vɔ … le). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): also 'still, already'. Gen 2:5

vueinɔnndo v. — frighten, terrify; be fearsome. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): be afraid (middle of 'fear'); variant wèènɔ̌ŋndó, also 'frighten people'. Other forms: vueinun, vueinunnin, vueinɔn. 1 Chr 12:9

vuɛɛndo n. (o) — woman; (vocative) woman!. Other forms: vuɛɛn. John 8:10

vuilen n. (len) — theft, stealing; thief. Exod 22:1

vuiyo n. (o), pl. vuiya — thief. Exod 22:1

vukɔɔ n. (o) — village meeting place for settling disputes. Keita 1979, p. 142; Lexique kissi–français, p. 63; Terminologie (histoire), n° 130

vulan n. — knees. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): knee (singular, le class). Variants: vuran (with r). Ezek 47:4

vulen n. (len), pl. vulan — knee. Keita 1979, p. 133; Paulme 1964, p. 122; Lexique kissi–français, p. 63

vulɔɔ v. — grow, sprout. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): also: thread a needle. Other forms: vul, vulnin. Gen 3:18

vulukɛlɛɛ adj. — multiform. Other forms: salabɔɔ, nɛilabɔɔbɔɔ. Terminologie (idéologie), n° 440

vulumo n., pl. vulumɔa — enemy of the witch (kuino). Paulme 1964, p. 122

vum ideo. — (ideophone) suddenly, with a start (pounding heart, fire flaring up). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): sound of slow regular beating (heartbeat), of a fire being lit. Gen 27:33

vundaa v. — rain continuously; all-day rain. Paulme 1964, p. 123; Lexique kissi–français, p. 63

vunduan n. (an) — shade, shadows (plural of vundulen); image (of a living person). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): plural (ma) of 'shade, shadow'; also the soul, an umbrella, an illustration. Other forms: vunduma. Judg 9:15

vundulen n. (len) — shadow, shade; vision; umbrella; image; spirit. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): shade, shadow; the soul of a person. Gen 15:1

vunno n., pl. vulla — dignitary of female initiation. Paulme 1964, p. 123

vunɔnndo v. — defend oneself; deny, refute. Other forms: vunun. Lexique kissi–français, p. 63

vuntele interj. — I greet (noble formula). Paulme 1964, p. 104

vuo v. — die. Other forms: vu, vunin, vi, vinin. Gen 43:8

vusalen n. — ballet. Terminologie (arts), n° 21

vusamba n. — calabash sistrum (instrument of initiated girls in the North). Paulme 1964, p. 123

vusuŋaa v. — erode. Other forms: vusuŋa. Lexique kissi–français, p. 63

vuulullo v. — inflict. Terminologie (histoire), n° 403

vuulu v. — throw (something) to (someone). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): throw to someone; shoot, thatch for someone. 2 Sam 20:21

vuuo1 v. — throw, cast; kick. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): throw (e.g. with a sling); thatch a roof; shoot. Other forms: vuu. Exod 4:3

vuuo2 v. — crawl. Other forms: vuu. Lexique kissi–français, p. 63

vuvo n. — epilepsy, catalepsy, trance. Paulme 1964, p. 123

vuyan-vuyan adv. — in disorder. Lexique kissi–français, p. 63

yaalanndo v. — condemn oneself. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): incriminate oneself. 1 Cor 11:29

yaalianndo v. — rebuke sharply, scold (to silence). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): frighten; shout to scare away birds; judge, find guilty. Matt 20:31

yààmàá v. — Southern Kissi only — yawn; wheeze. Childs 2000, p. 394

yaamɔɔlen n. (len) — enmity, hostility, hatred. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): hatred, jealousy. Eph 2:14

yaamɔɔ n. (o), pl. yaamɔaa — enemy. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): enemy, someone hated. Exod 23:4

yáánáná ideo. — Southern Kissi only — weak, listless, downcast. Childs 2000, p. 395

yàándɔɔ num. — third. Other forms: yàándɔlen, yàándɔ. Gen 14:4

yáásàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — plant species with edible leaves. Childs 2000, p. 395

yáàù ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (yanking out). Childs 2000, p. 396

yààwàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — sword grass (swamps). Childs 2000, p. 396

yààwèí n. (i), pl. yààwǎŋ — Southern Kissi only — onion. Childs 2000, p. 396

yààwìǎŋndó v. — Southern Kissi only — peel. Childs 2000, p. 396

yààyàá1 n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — snake species. Childs 2000, p. 396

yààyàá2 v. — Southern Kissi only — augment, amplify (a case); celebrate (returning initiates). Childs 2000, p. 396

yaayɛi n. (i) — bells, iron rattles, strung small bells. Terminologie (arts), n° 132

yaa v. — send. Lexique kissi–français, p. 63

yàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — snake species. Childs 2000, p. 394

yáá num. — three. Gen 2:19

yabibio n. (o) — pineapple. Keita 1979, p. 140; Paulme 1964, p. 125 (K); Lexique kissi–français, p. 63

yákólàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — large monkey. Childs 2000, p. 396

yalaa n. (o), pl. yalalan — net; placenta. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): round scoop net used by women for fishing; mosquito net. Ps 25:15

yàlàá n. (o) — lion. Gen 49:9

yàlàbàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — deceit, lying. Childs 2000, p. 397

yálábóndáá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — frog species; rainbow. Childs 2000, p. 397

yàláfùlòó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — poisonous snake. Childs 2000, p. 397

yalahiniaa n. (o) — hammock. Keita 1979, p. 159

yàlàkánáá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — lion. Childs 2000, p. 397

yalalen n. (len) — deceit (in speech), treachery. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): gossip, slander. Rom 3:13

yalama n. — housewife; matron. Paulme 1964, p. 125; Lexique kissi–français, p. 63

yálánndo n. (o) — oak, great tree. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): a tree species. Other forms: yálán, yálánnde. Gen 35:8

yalantaalaa n. (o) — calabash cup. Keita 1979, p. 159

yalanyaalaa n. — calabash. Lexique kissi–français, p. 63

yala v. — (auxiliary, always negative: yala X le) not yet, not soon; be slow to. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): spend a while doing (defective verb, used in the negative). Exod 34:6

yǎlbándíláá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — illness closing the entrance of the vagina. Childs 2000, p. 397

yallo n. (o) — fetish; scarecrow; yallo cult. Keita 1979, p. 150; Paulme 1964, p. 125; Lexique kissi–français, p. 63; Terminologie (idéologie), n° 294

yalɔɔ v. — shout, exclaim. Other forms: yalu. Variants: yarɔɔ (with r), yaru. Lexique kissi–français, p. 64; Sandara Kisia, fable 4

yàmáfìkóó n. (o), pl. yàmáfìkóláŋ — Southern Kissi only — swing; sling. Childs 2000, p. 397

yàmátàndíó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — bird species that calls other birds to the rice. Childs 2000, p. 397

yambaa n. — tobacco. Lexique kissi–français, p. 63

yàmbàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — raffia skirt. Childs 2000, p. 397

yambalekale n. — plant (species) whose root is used in indigo dyeing. Paulme 1964, p. 125

yambalen n. (len) — cassava (tuber). Lexique kissi–français, p. 63

yamba n. — charm (koma) that stops the rain. Paulme 1964, p. 125

yambele folalen n. — cassava. Keita 1979, p. 140

yambɛi n. — tubers; cassava. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): tuber (generic): cassava, eddo, yam. Keita 1979, p. 140; Paulme 1964, p. 125; Sandara Kisia, proverbe 64

yambɔɔ v. — lay down, put to bed, lay; (yambaa) lie; hospitalize (a sick person); spread out (a mat, a sheet). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): set, lay down; also lay (a road), operate on someone. Other forms: yambu, yambun, yambunin, yambaa. Gen 28:11

yambulɛn n. — dash. Terminologie (langue), n° 404

yambullo n. — theatre. Terminologie (arts), n° 283

yambulnɔɔ n. — actor, actress. Terminologie (arts), n° 2

yamɛi n. (i) — judgement, justice, case. Gen 18:25

yanama n. — sinner (catechism). Paulme 1964, p. 125

yàndìá v. — Southern Kissi only — weave; unroll (cloth, ball, string). Childs 2000, p. 398

yandɔɔ1 n. (o) — flower. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): (verb) to flower, blossom, bear fruit. Exod 9:31

yandɔɔ2 v. — flower, blossom. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): flower, produce flowers. Other forms: yandu, yendu, yandunin. Exod 9:31

yàndɔ̀ɔ́ n. (o), pl. yàndɔ̀ɔ̀láŋ — Southern Kissi only — young, newly formed fruit. Childs 2000, p. 398

yandulen n. (len) — spiny palm-like tree (trunk used for rice containers). Lexique kissi–français, p. 63

yàndúléŋ n. (le) — Southern Kissi only — trigger (of a gun). Childs 2000, p. 398

yandule n. — trophy made of a dead chief's severed arm. Paulme 1964, p. 126

yangaa1 n. — shrimp, crayfish. Keita 1979, p. 27

yangaa2 v. — delay, linger; spend the morning (a yangaa kɛndɛ: greeting used mid-morning, 9-11 a.m.). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): spend or pass the morning. Acts 9:38

yangbaa n. — concert. Terminologie (arts), n° 69

yankɔlo n. — dance before circumcision. Paulme 1964, p. 126

yanlaninɔɔ n. — listener. Terminologie (langue), n° 45

yanɔnndo v. — spread out, stretch out. Other forms: yanun, yenun. Lexique kissi–français, p. 64

yáŋgbàŋ ideo. — Southern Kissi only — wide open, widely. Childs 2000, p. 398

yàŋgbâŋ- adj. — Southern Kissi only — wide. Childs 2000, p. 398

yàŋìlàá n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — traditional skirt (worn by men and women). Childs 2000, p. 398

yaŋnun v. — listen to, heed. Other forms: yaŋnɔnndo. Exod 6:12

yaŋɔɔlen n. (len), pl. yaŋɔɔlan — trap, snare; fish trap; ambush. Other forms: yaŋɔɔle. Job 22:10

yaŋɔɔ v. — lend (an ear), listen (yaŋ nilan); set (a trap). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): set a trap; prick up one's ears, listen carefully. Other forms: yaŋ. Gen 27:8

yàɲáŋndó n. (o) — Southern Kissi only — watery swamp full of brush. Childs 2000, p. 398

yasaa n. (o), pl. yasalan — ear of grain. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): bunch, ear (of maize), stalk, clump. Mark 4:8

yasabaa diliŋaa n. — concentration camp. Terminologie (histoire), n° 131

yasabaa n. (o) — shelter, camp; workshop. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): temporary cooking site on a farm, before the farm kitchen is built. Isa 28:15

yasaba baalaa n. — building site. Terminologie (arts), n° 47

yàsáŋ-bělló n. — Southern Kissi only — bunch of palm nuts. Childs 2000, p. 399

yasiaa v. — scratch the ground (fowl); rummage, search; tease; dance; peck; sift. Lexique kissi–français, p. 64

yaspe n. — jasper. Exod 28:20

yati adv. — really, truly. Lexique kissi–français, p. 64

yàùwà- adj. — Southern Kissi only — cooking, used for cooking. Childs 2000, p. 399

yáù ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (dragging quickly, yanking). Childs 2000, p. 399

yavaa n., pl. yavalan — divination (vanaa viamaa yavaa 'diviners, magicians'). Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): a potion used to uncover the truth or foretell; a fortune teller's parcel. Gen 41:8

yava n. — weed (species) of rice fields. Paulme 1964, p. 126

yave n., pl. yava — onion. Paulme 1964, p. 126

yàwàá v. — Southern Kissi only — take away, remove, snatch. Childs 2000, p. 400

yàwǎŋndó v. — Southern Kissi only — peel off. Childs 2000, p. 400

yáwèlè-yáwèlè ideo. — Southern Kissi only — (food badly cooked, overdone). Childs 2000, p. 400

yáwlen n. (len) — belt, sash; girls' belt of blue beads; amulet made of the first cut hair. Exod 28:4

yawnun v. — be cooked, be boiled. Southern Kissi (Childs 2000): be cooked, get hot, cook by itself. Lev 6:21

yawvo divioo v. — tan (hides). Terminologie (arts), n° 275

yawvo v. — cook. Other forms: yaw. Gen 25:29

docs.title: Glossary of grammatical terms
docs.text:
Terms used in this guide, with their French equivalent.

Term French Definition agreement accord Repetition of a noun's class on the words that accompany it. See Agreement. benefactive bénéfactif Derived verb showing that the action is done for someone: dimul “say to”. causative causatif Derived verb meaning “make do, make be”: hivia “make pass”. circumposition circumposition Preposition and postposition framing a noun: o … nin “in”. class pronoun pronom de classe Pronoun that refers back to a noun according to its class: le, la, ma. class referent référent de classe Class suffix repeated at the end of a relative clause: fula-o. class suffix terminaison de classe End of the noun that shows its class and number: -ndo, -lan, -len… full form forme pleine Noun with its class suffix: cɛiyo. habitual habituel Aspect of habitual or general action. ideophone idéophone Expressive word that depicts a sound or a manner: púŋ, few-few. long form, verbal noun forme longue Form of the verb ending like a noun (tosaa), used after co, va. long vowel voyelle longue Vowel pronounced for longer, written double: aa, ɔɔ. middle moyen Derived verb with a reflexive or passive meaning: cɔmnun “show oneself”. noun class classe nominale Group of nouns that have the same suffix and the same agreements. See Noun classes. particle particule Small invariable word with a grammatical function: ni, le, yɛ. perfective accompli Aspect that presents the action as completed: I tuei “I have heard”. postposition postposition Relational word placed after the noun: coo “on”, nin “in”. progressive progressif Aspect of action in progress: co / va + long form. relative clause relative Clause that modifies a noun: lɔma ya sɔl-lan “the dream that I had”. stem radical Part of the word that carries the meaning, without a suffix. stem form forme radicale Noun without a suffix, before a determiner: cɛi kon. subjunctive subjonctif Mood of purpose and wish: mò + verb. tone ton Pitch of the voice on a syllable, which can change the meaning. See Tone.

docs.title: Grammatical terms in Kisiei
docs.text:
In the 1970s the Académie des langues in Conakry proposed Kisiei terms for teaching grammar (Académie des Langues s.d.). They are given here respelled in the Bible's orthography. Some are ordinary words used in a technical sense (diomndo "voice, sound" for tone, tumndo "base, stump" for stem, diolan "name, noun"); the others are coinages not found in the Bible. They are proposals; how far they are used today remains to be checked.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
• Verb tables: the forms of regular and irregular verbs and of the verb “be”;
  • Kisiei–English dictionary: the whole lexicon in alphabetical order;
  • English–Kisiei index: find a Kisiei word from English;
  • Word lists: the same vocabulary arranged by field of meaning;
  • Common phrases: greeting, thanking, answering, asking for information;
  • Glossary: the grammatical terms used in this guide;
  • Open questions: points to be checked with speakers.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text: These points cannot be settled from the written sources alone: the Bible (BKG) does not mark everything (in particular tones), the 1979 description (Keita 1979) is sometimes incomplete or contradicted by the Bible, and Childs's description (Childs 1995) concerns Southern Kissi. They are put to speakers and teachers; all observations are welcome (see the project repository).

docs.title: Spelling
docs.text:
1. Tones. Which tones should be marked, apart from the grammatical cases where the Bible marks them regularly (mí / mì, háá, ndóò, tùú)? The lexical tones of common words are not described anywhere for the Kisiei of Guinea. See Tone.
  2. Alphabetical order. The order proposed in this guide for ɛ, ɔ, ŋ, ɲ and the digraphs needs to be validated. See Alphabet.
  3. Words not in the Bible. The respelled 1979 forms (status Respelled) must be confirmed one by one, in particular vowel length and the final nasal (n or ŋ).

docs.title: Nouns and determiners
docs.text:
1. Near and far in the an, len, lan classes. According to the 1979 description, man, len, lan are used for “this…” and “that…”, distinguished by tone (Keita 1979, p. 58). To be checked.
  2. Irregular plurals. The 1979 list of irregular plurals (Keita 1979, p. 26-29) needs to be completed and checked.
  3. 1st and 2nd person plural possessives for the i and -on classes: forms not found in the Bible.
  4. 1979 indefinites kèkè “any” and yööli “all”, not found in the Bible: do they still exist, and how should they be written?
  5. 1979 interrogatives köè and ngö “which”, not found in the Bible.
  6. Negating a noun. In Southern Kissi, the negated noun in “it is not X” takes its class pronoun (Childs 1995, p. 261-262). Is this the case in the Kisiei of Guinea?

docs.title: Verb
docs.text:
1. Tone of the perfective and the habitual. These two forms differ only in tone (Keita 1979, p. 95); a precise description of verbal tones is lacking.
  2. Stems of “go”. The Bible uses kɔa in narrative and kɔɛ after mì; the 1979 description gives köè in the past and köa in the habitual. Which of the two distributions is that of everyday usage?
  3. The particle -lɔ / -ndɔ / -yɔ. Its use for politeness is clear (yaŋ-ndɔ), but the Bible also uses it in negative sentences in the past (ndóò vil-lɔ … le Gen 2:5). What is this second use?
  4. Reciprocal. The 1979 description gives long forms -anndo, -lanndo (yilanndo), not found in the Bible.
  5. Future with co and future with -nin. What difference in meaning do speakers make between n co ndu dio and dianin?

docs.title: Varieties
docs.text:
1. Regional variants. The handwritten notes mention Kissidougou variants (r for l, other words). Which of them should be part of a common written usage? See Regional varieties.

  2. Dictionary variants. The dictionary now gives, after the headword, Guéckédou and Kissidougou variants (from Paulme and the handwritten notes) and r pronunciations (from the Lexique). They need to be confirmed one by one.

docs.title: Older northern sources
docs.text:
Questions raised by comparing the Bible with the older sources: Paulme's vocabulary and texts (Paulme 1964), the Lexique kissi–français (Lexique kissi – français s.d.) and the fables Sandara Kissia (Mission Protestante de Kissidougou s.d.).

  1. "But" and "because". Sandara Kissia constantly uses kɔnɔ "but" and katu "because", which the Bible never uses. Are they current in speech, and should they be written this way? See Prepositions and conjunctions.
  2. Prohibition without le. Paulme records la kɛrania "one must not travel" without the final negative particle, whereas the Bible has it (La kɔa lon te Num 14:42).
  3. Negative future. Paulme writes ɔ kwani sɔre "he will not leave tomorrow", with the vowel of the affirmative future; the Bible has kuenin te.
  4. Auxiliary "can". Paulme uses kɛy as an auxiliary (i kɛy pundɔ re "I could not buy"), a form the Bible does not have in this sense.
  5. The stem in e / ɛ (de, kɔɛ). The 1979 description calls it "past"; in the Bible it is the stem of the subjunctive and the condition. See Stems and groups.
  6. Possessor before the noun. Paulme gives the order possessor + noun (sando dolã "the hare's name") as the general rule; the Bible uses it too, but how far? See Possessives.
  7. "We two". Paulme describes min as an inclusive "we"; the Bible gives no clear example.
  8. Suffix -le "with". Paulme analyses mallole as "with the stranger"; this -le could be the final negation le.
  9. Near or far? The Lexique translates kpɛlun and macɛlu as "near"; the Bible uses kpɛɛlun for "near" but contrasts these words with "far" in a way that remains to be clarified (Isa 57:19).
  10. "Four" or "nine"? Paulme translates nɔma nwɔlu as "four", but the word is built like "nine" (5 + 4), as ŋɔmahiɔɔlu in the Bible. A translation slip or another usage? See Numerals.
  11. Plant names. Several trees recorded by Paulme (dolio, kpallo, lollo) resemble Southern Kissi names (Childs 2000): are they the same species?

docs.title: Common phrases
docs.text: A few common phrases, all taken from the Kisiei Bible (BKG). They show the spelling and the construction; in conversation, polite formulas may vary from region to region.

docs.text:
Kisiei English Reference Nɔm nɛ̀ɛ́-nɛ̀? Who are you? Gen 27:32 Ya Esau ni I am Esau. Gen 27:32 Kuɛɛ niaa fula yɛ? Where do you come from? Gen 29:4 Haran naa n fula ni We come from Haran. Gen 29:4 Vɛ̀ɛ̀ o co kɛndɛ lon? Is he well? Gen 29:6 Kuɛɛ nɛ n co yɛ? Where are you? Gen 3:9

For other everyday greetings, see the dialogues in the 1979 description (in the old spelling) (Keita 1979); forms that do not appear in the Bible must be checked with speakers.

docs.title: Older formulas and proverbs
docs.text:
The Bible uses La lɔl kɛndɛ "farewell, stay well" when taking leave (Acts 15:29). In the 1940s Denise Paulme recorded lɔ kɛnde "goodbye, good night" and a lɔ kɛnde "good morning", answered with nyɛnyɛre "fine" (Paulme 1964, p. 42, 72), and the question a lɔl kɛnde "did you sleep well?" (Paulme 1964, p. 58).

Proverbs and riddles, respelled in the Bible's orthography, are collected in the appendix Tales, proverbs and riddles; texts about everyday life (cooking, farm work, prayers) in Denise Paulme's texts.

Note

The 1979 description gives complete tables for sixteen verbs, with all six persons (Keita 1979, p. 96-109), in the old spelling; the description of Southern Kissi gives the paradigms of cimbu “leave” and kiol “bite” (Childs 1995, p. 220-221). For “go”, Paulme records in the 1940s ma kwa “they go”, ɔ kwani “he will leave”, ɔ kwɛ “he has left” (Paulme 1964, p. 48), that is kɔa, kɔanin, kɔɛ. The tables above keep only the forms checked in the Bible.

docs.title: Word lists
docs.text: These lists are generated automatically from the project's lexicon (6650 entries). Words are grouped by semantic domain following the SIL Semantic Domains classification; a word may appear in several domains. Attested words link to their first occurrence in the Kisiei Bible; Confirmed words are not in the Bible but confirmed by a speaker; Respelled words come from an older written source (Keita 1979, Paulme 1964, the Lexique kissi–français, the Académie terminology, Sandara Kisia), converted to the current spelling; they still need confirmation; Southern Kissi words are known only from the Southern Kissi dictionary (Childs 2000): they are not attested in the North and are spelled as Childs writes them. The lexicon is also available as CSV, TSV, LIFT (for FieldWorks) and CLDF.

docs.title: Archive
docs.text: The archive/ folder of the repository keeps older documents on Kisiei: those on which this guide is based, and other sources (word lists, texts, lists of terms) still to be used. Most are scanned typescripts that predate the current spelling: they are not a spelling model, and anything taken from them is checked against the Bible.

docs.title: Sékou Sondo Keita and the Académie des langues
docs.text: Document Contents Kissie fondamental (scan) Scan (189 pages) of Sékou Sondo Keita's thesis, Essai d'élaboration d'un kisiei fondamental à l'usage des locuteurs non kisi, Institut polytechnique Gamal Abdel Nasser de Conakry, 1979. Kissie fondamental (transcription) Full transcription in Markdown, in the original spelling; the handwritten corrections are incorporated. This transcription is final and will not be converted to the current spelling. Kissie fondamental (handwritten notes) Handwritten annotations by later readers, page by page: translations, French glosses, Kissidougou variants (Annotations manuscrites portées sur l'exemplaire numérisé de Keita (1979) s.d.). Kissie fondamental (annex) The thesis annex, Contes, proverbes, devinettes (typescript pp. 166–184), found separately and missing from the main scan: 18 pages of Kisiei tales, each followed by proverbs (talelan) and riddles (budon pialan), with handwritten French glosses (Keita 1979). Notes: every proverb and riddle as typed, and an outline of each tale. Terminology: language, arts, history, ideology Four lists from the Académie des langues (Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research): numbered French terms with their Kisiei translation, for language and grammar (16 pp.), the arts (12 pp.), history and politics (21 pp.), ideology, economy and society (13 pp.) (Académie des Langues s.d.). The pages name no author; the attribution to Keita comes from the file names. Transcriptions: language, arts, history, ideology (the scan starts at no. 249). Nouvelle orthographe kissi Correspondence sheet between the old and the new spelling (Nouvelle orthographe kissi (tableau de correspondances) s.d.).

docs.title: Denise Paulme
docs.text: Document Contents Documents sur la langue kissi Documents sur la langue kissi : lexique et textes (Paulme 1964), 173 pages, printed from the University of Florida Digital Collections. Vocabulary and texts collected by the ethnologist Denise Paulme during two stays in the Kissi country with André Schaeffner (October 1945 – June 1946, October 1948 – May 1949), around Kissidougou and Guéckédou; with a bibliography of earlier work on Kissi. Full transcription (lexicon and all eleven texts, with interlinear glosses and notes). Kissi vocabulaire Another copy of the same work (151 pages), scanned from a typescript, with a few handwritten notes.

docs.title: Other documents
docs.text: Document Contents Lexique kissi – français Alphabetical Kisiei–French word list of 68 pages, author unknown, typed in the current spelling (ɛ, ɔ), with handwritten additions (Lexique kissi – français s.d.). Transcription. Sandara Kissia Sandara Kissia: fables des Kissiens (Mission Protestante de Kissidougou s.d.), Protestant Mission, Kissidougou, undated: twenty fables in Kisiei, followed by 83 proverbs and riddles (taleraŋ) with their explanation. Scan (24 pages) and a full transcription as an EPUB. Older missionary spelling (ty for c, no tones): words taken from it are respelled to the Bible's orthography.

docs.title: How to cite the 1979 manual
docs.text:
The page numbers cited (“Keita 1979, p. 57”) are those of the typescript. In the transcription, each page begins with a link to the handwritten notes for that page (“✎ Handwritten notes, p. 57”), which makes it easy to find the passage.

The spelling of quotations from 1979 is that of the original (tyo, nh, è, ö…); the Old and new spelling page explains how to read it.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
This guide relies on three sets of sources, in this order of authority:

  1. The Kisiei Bible (BKG), the standard for spelling and usage;
  2. Keita's manual (Keita 1979) and its handwritten annotations, the basic description of the grammar;
  3. Childs's grammar and dictionary (Childs 1995, 2000), a description of Southern Kissi, for comparison.

The Sources and the standard page explains this choice.

  • Bibliography: all the references cited;
  • Archive: the documents kept in the repository;
  • Tools: the list of Bible words, the concordance and the automatic checks.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text: The rules of this guide are drawn from the texts of the Kisiei Bible (BKG) with the help of a few tools, available in the tools/ folder of the repository. They are run with uv.

docs.title: The Bible text
docs.text:
tools/fetch_bible.py downloads the chapters of the Kisiei Bible from bible.com, slowly (about one per second), into a local .cache/bible/ folder that is not added to the repository: the text remains the property of the Alliance Biblique en Guinée. Only the list of word forms is published.

uv run tools/fetch_bible.py --delay 1.0

docs.title: The list of word forms
docs.text: tools/build_wordlist.py produces references/bible-bkg-wordforms.tsv: each word form of the Bible (ignoring tones and capitals), its number of occurrences, its spellings with tone accents and a first reference. The complete Bible (1,188 chapters) contains about 939,000 words and nearly 22,000 different forms.

docs.title: The concordance
docs.text:
tools/bible_concordance.py searches the local text for a word, part of a word or a pattern, and shows each occurrence in its context with its reference. It is the main tool for checking a rule:

uv run tools/bible_concordance.py -w "ndɔ(ɔ|a|lan|len)"

docs.title: The automatic checks
docs.text:
Every time the site is built (mkdocs build --strict), a module (tools/kisiei_hooks.py):

  • checks that every Kisiei example marked as attested is in the list of Bible word forms; otherwise, the build fails;
  • turns citations (“(Keita 1979, p. 57)”) into links to the bibliography and reports unknown keys;
  • also accepts an abbreviation in double square brackets (book code, chapter and verse, for example GEN.1.3) for a Bible reference, but the pages write references as plain Markdown links to the verse on bible.com ([Gen 1:3](https://www.bible.com/bible/1394/GEN.1.3.BKG)), which are also readable outside the site.

tools/check_i18n.py checks that every page exists in French and in English.
